BURHAN:v4p36/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p36/r3.speaker: ثعلب والمبرد
BURHAN:v4p36/r3.claim: Tha'lab and al-Mubarrad say the pronouns in فيهم and منهم refer respectively to the People of the Cave and the Jews.
BURHAN:v4p36/r3.anchor: والهاء والميم في منهم لليهود قاله ثعلب والمبرد

ITQAN:v2p381/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p381/r19.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p381/r19.anchor:
﴿ شاكلته ﴾ ناحيته
2501 ﴿ رجما ﴾ ظنا
2502 ﴿ ملتحدا ﴾ ملجأ

QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r2.claim: Surface readers among Jews and Muslims speculate about the sleepers’ number; the few who know are verified knowers, and the wording points to seven.
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r2.anchor: الظاهريون من أهل الكتاب والمسلمين الذين لا علم لهم بالحقائق

QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r3.claim: The conjunction before the eighth dog signals a quality inseparable from its subject, and the phrase that only a few know confirms seven without a further number.
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r3.anchor: وتوسيط الواو الدالة على أن الصفة مجامعة للموصوف ولا تفارقه

QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r4.claim: In the inward reading, the seven sleepers represent the theoretical and practical intellects, thought, estimation, imagination, memory, and common sense; the dog is the lower self, while sun and spirit apply in both readings.
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r4.anchor: فهم العاقلتان: النظرية والعملية، والفكر والوهم، والتخيل والذكر

QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r5.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r5.claim: A report says the seven comprised three on the king’s right, three on his left, and a seventh shepherd who owned the dog.
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r5.anchor: إنهم كانوا سبعة، ثلاثة عن يمين الملك وثلاثة عن يساره، والسابع هو الراعي

QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r6.claim: If sound, the report maps the king to the commanding self; the right-hand advisers to the two intellects and thought; the left-hand advisers to imagination, estimation, and memory; and the shepherd to common sense over the senses.
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r6.anchor: فالملك هو دقيانوس النفس الأمارة، والثلاثة الذين كانوا عن يمينه يستشيرهم

QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r7.claim: On this reading, the three-count includes the heart and two intellects; the five-count adds thought and estimation but omits common sense and memory as passive repositories.
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r7.anchor: والذين قالوا هم ثلاثة ارادوا القلب والعاقلتين، والذين قالوا خمسة زادوا عليهم

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p25/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p25/r4.speaker: ابن محيصن
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p25/r4.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin alone assimilates the thāʾ of ثلات into the tāʾ of رابعهم; their nearby articulation points license the assimilation despite the preceding alif.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p25/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة ابن محيصن: "ثلات رابعهم كلبهم7"

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr alone has a report with fatḥa on the mīm of خمسة; the author attributes it to transmitted usage, perhaps following the preceding عشرة.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r1.anchor: إلا ابن كثير وحده في رواية حسن بن محمد2 عن شبل

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r2.claim: The unusual vowel should not be dismissed as poetic necessity: Arabic place names can have variant forms, as the report about ركك and ركا illustrates.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r2.anchor: أتعرف رككا هذا؟ فقال: قد كان ههنا ماء يسمى "ركا"

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r1.claim: God conceals His saints from outsiders through protective jealousy; only intimates sharing their state recognize them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r1.anchor: فهم في كتم الغيرة وإيواء الستر

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r2.speaker: شيوخ هذه الطائفة
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r2.claim: Sufi masters describe the Sufis as one household into which outsiders do not enter.

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r3.claim: Those who do not know the saints' condition cannot be consulted about it; a heart without love for the beloveds cannot remember them truly.
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r3.anchor: فلا يصح استفتاء من غاب علمهم عنه في حالهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r1.claim: Quraysh sent al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith and ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ to Jewish scholars, who proposed questions about the youths, a world-traveling man, and the spirit as a test of Muhammad’s prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r1.anchor: وسبب نزولها أن قريشا بعثت النضر بن الحارث وعقبة بن أبي معيط إلى أحبار اليهود بالمدينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r2.claim: A second report says the Jews judged that answering all three questions would disprove prophethood, while answering two and withholding the other would confirm it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r2.anchor: وروي في هذا السبب أن اليهود قالت: إن أجابكم عن الثلاثة فليس بنبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r4.claim: The sura’s opening connects to the prior sura’s affirmation of true revelation and humility: praise God for the upright warning Quran, which warns those asserting a son and promises believers reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r4.anchor: ومناسبة أول هذه السورة لآخر ما قبلها أنه لما قال وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r6.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r6.claim: Al-Māwardī says سيقولون refers to the disputants previously mentioned, whose disagreement about the youths’ number preceded their discovery.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في سيقولون عائد على من تقدم ذكرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Christians of Najrān debated the count with the Prophet: the denominations gave the first, second, and third numbers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: يعود على نصارى نجران تناظروا مع الرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī assigns the first number to the Jacobite Sayyid, the second to the Nestorian ʿĀqib, and the correct third to Muslims, who learned it through Gabriel’s revelation to the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r8.anchor: وفي الكشاف أن السيد قال الجملة الأولى وكان يعقوبيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r9.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r9.claim: ʿAlī reportedly names the seven youths Tamlikha, Makshalbīnā, Mashalbīnā, Marnūsh, Dabarnūsh, Shādhānūsh, and a shepherd; they fled Daqyānūs from Ephesus, and their dog was Qiṭmīr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r9.anchor: وعن علي هم سبعة نفر أسماؤهم تمليخا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the pronoun refers to contemporary People of the Torah, who differed over the youths’ number.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عطية الضمير في قوله سيقولون يراد به أهل التوراة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r1.claim: The future sīn compresses omitted dialogue: after the Prophet tells the cave story, he is to ask their number, and they will answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r1.anchor: وجاء بسين الاستقبال لأنه كأنه في الكلام طي وإدماج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r2.speaker: ابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r2.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin assimilates the ث of ثلاث into ت because the sounds are close and both voiceless, with a preceding vowel-letter facilitating assimilation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن ثلاث بإدغام الثاء في التاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r3.claim: The later يقولون forms lack sīn because coordination places them under the first future, or because the verb itself can carry a future sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r3.anchor: ويقولون لم يأت بالسين فيه ولا فيما بعده لأنه معطوف على المستقبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r4.speaker: شبل بن عباد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r4.claim: Shibl b. ʿAbbād, from Ibn Kathīr, reads خَمْسة with open mīm, a dialect also found in عشرة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r4.anchor: وقرأ شبل بن عباد عن ابن كثير بفتح ميم خمسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r5.speaker: ابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r5.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads خِمْسة with kasra on both khāʾ and mīm and assimilates tāʾ into sīn; another report assimilates tanwīn without nasalization.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن بكسر الخاء والميم وبإدغام التاء في السين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r6.claim: رجما بالغيب means shooting at what is hidden, hence guessing; the throwing image suggests repeated attempts to hit an unknown target, and the root also appears in ترجمان and ترجمة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r6.anchor: رجما بالغيب رميا بالشيء المغيب عنهم أو ظنا، استعير من الرجم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r7.speaker: زهير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r7.claim: Zuhayr’s line about war being known and tasted, not merely conjectured, attests that مرجم means supposed or guessed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r7.anchor: وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتم ... وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r8.claim: Calling the first two counts رجما بالغيب marks them as guesses; the unqualified third statement is signaled as true, as reported from ʿAlī and the Prophet through Gabriel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r8.anchor: قائل تلك المقالتين لم يقولوا ذلك عن علم وإنما قالوا ذلك على سبيل التخمين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r9.claim: رجما may be a verbal noun for an omitted verb, an object of a verb understood to include conjecturing, or a purpose phrase explaining their guess.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r9.anchor: وانتصب رجما على أنه مصدر لفعل مضمر أي يرجمون بذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r10.claim: ثلاثة is a predicate of an omitted subject, understood as three persons; رابعهم says the dog completes their number as fourth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r10.anchor: وثلاثة خبر مبتدأ محذوف، والجملة بعده صفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r11.claim: وَثامنهم coordinates a second sentence: first they assert seven, then separately say their dog is eighth, which signals affirmation unlike the earlier single descriptive clauses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r11.anchor: والواو في وثامنهم للعطف على الجملة السابقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r12.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش وابن خالويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r12.claim: Abū Bakr b. ʿAyyāsh and Ibn Khālawayh call the wāw a ‘wāw of eight,’ claiming Quraysh inserted it when counting from six to eight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r12.anchor: وذكر عن أبي بكر بن عياش وابن خالويه أنها واو الثمانية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r13.claim: A reading وثامنهم كالبهم means ‘their dog’s owner’; some infer eight youths and understand كلبهم with an omitted possessive noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r13.anchor: وقرىء وثامنهم كالبهم أي صاحب كلبهم، وزعم بعضهم أنهم ثمانية رجال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r14.claim: Some commentators make وثامنهم a divine aside rather than part of the quoted claim; on that reading, God’s statement confirms seven youths plus their dog.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r14.anchor: وذهب بعض المفسرين إلى أن قوله وثامنهم ليس داخلا تحت قولهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r15.claim: Most Companions, Successors, and leading exegetes hold that the group numbered seven youths and an eighth, their dog.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p159/r15.anchor: وأما رابعهم كلبهم وسادسهم كلبهم فهو من جملة المحكي من قولهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the wāw introduces a clause describing an indefinite noun or a circumstantial clause about a definite one, reinforcing a stable attribute; it shows the seven-and-dog claim was confident, not conjectural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r1.anchor: هي الواو التي تدخل على الجملة الواقعة صفة للنكرة كما تدخل على الواقعة حالا عن المعرفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says grammarians do not recognize a wāw that links a clause as an adjective to make the quality more fixed; coordinated simple adjectives require distinct meanings, and clauses are even less suited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r2.anchor: وكون الواو تدخل على الجملة الواقعة صفة دالة على لصوق الصفة بالموصوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r3.claim: He rejects treating the clause in 15:4 as adjectival evidence: it is circumstantial, and no grammarian licenses an adjective like مررت برجل ويأكل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r3.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى إلا ولها فالجملة حالية ويكفي ردا لقول الزمخشري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r4.claim: Only God has complete knowledge of the youths’ number, while a few people may know what God reveals; divine all-knowingness and limited human knowledge do not conflict.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161/r4.anchor: والمثبت في حق الله تعالى هو الأعلمية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says, ‘I am among the few.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أنا من القليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r2.claim: The command not to dispute their number answers the People of Scripture’s wrangling; ظاهر means stick to revealed information without humiliating or scolding them, consistent with 16:125.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r2.anchor: وقيده بقوله ظاهرا أي غير متعمق فيه وهو إن نقص عليهم ما أوحي إليك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says to tell them plainly, ‘It is not as you know.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: مراء ظاهرا هو قولك لهم ليس كما تعلمون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r4.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r4.claim: Al-Māwardī interprets the command as allowing debate only with clear proof.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the permitted debate is certain and grounded in knowledge of the true report God revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: إلا جدال متيقن عالم بحقيقة الخبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r6.speaker: ابن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r6.claim: Ibn Baḥr takes ظاهرا to mean a debate witnessed by people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: ظاهرا يشهده الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r7.speaker: التبريزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r7.claim: Al-Tabrīzī takes ظاهرا as a debate that defeats the opponent by proof, supported by Zuhayr’s use of ظاهر for something whose blame is gone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r7.anchor: وقال التبريزي: ظاهرا ذاهبا بحجة الخصم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r8.claim: The Prophet is told not to ask anyone from the People of Scripture about the story: neither to challenge them, which conflicts with gracious debate, nor to seek guidance, since revelation already guides him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r8.anchor: ثم نهاه أن يسأل أحدا من أهل الكتاب عن قصتهم

AKHFASH:v2p429/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p429/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p429/r3.claim: ما يعلمهم إلا قليل means only a few people know their number; the noun people is understood.
AKHFASH:v2p429/r3.anchor: أي: ما يعلمهم من الناس إلا قليل. والقليل يعلمونهم.

FARRA:v2p137/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p137/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v2p137/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sleepers numbered seven with their dog as the eighth.
FARRA:v2p137/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانوا سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم

FARRA:v2p137/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p137/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v2p137/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas counts himself among the few who know their number, as described in the verse.
FARRA:v2p137/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أنا من القليل الذين قال الله عز وجل

FARRA:v2p137/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p137/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p137/r9.claim: The instruction not to dispute except by what is apparent means to tell only what the Quran has made clear.
FARRA:v2p137/r9.anchor: يا محمد (إلا مراء ظاهرا) إلا أن تحدثهم به حديثا

FARRA:v2p138/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p138/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p138/r1.claim: The people from whom the Prophet was forbidden to seek an answer were Christians of Najran, split into Jacobite and Nestorian groups who had asked him their number.
FARRA:v2p138/r1.anchor: وهم فريقان أتوه من أهل نجران: يعقوبي ونسطوري

NAHHAS:v2p451/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p451/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p451/r14.claim: The statements ‘three’ and ‘their fourth was their dog,’ and the corresponding ‘sixth’ and ‘eighth’ clauses, have omitted subjects and subject-predicate structure.
NAHHAS:v2p451/r14.anchor: على اضمار مبتدأ أي هم ثلاثة ^ ( رابعهم كلبهم ) ^ مبتدأ وخبر ، وكذا ^ ( سادسهم كلبهم ) ^ ^ ( وثامنهم كلبهم

NAHHAS:v2p451/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p451/r15.speaker: قولان
NAHHAS:v2p451/r15.claim: One view says adding or omitting the wāw changes nothing; another says it marks completion and a shift from reported guesses to the truth that the dog was eighth.
NAHHAS:v2p451/r15.anchor: خاصة دون ما تقدم قولان : أحدهما أن دخولها وخروجها واحد

NAHHAS:v2p451/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p451/r16.speaker: إبراهيم بن السري
NAHHAS:v2p451/r16.claim: He reports the view that wāw marks the end of the story and the transition to the true count.
NAHHAS:v2p451/r16.anchor: ذكر هذا القول إبراهيم بن السري فيكون المعنى عليه أن الله جل وعز خبر بما يقولون ثم أتى بحقيقة الأمر فقال : وثامنهم كلبهم

NAHHAS:v2p451/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p451/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p451/r17.claim: The phrase ‘none know them except a few’ means a few people know their number; the verb raises the subject ‘few.’
NAHHAS:v2p451/r17.anchor: ما يعلمهم إلا قليل ) ^ رفع بفعله أي القليل يعلمونهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p459/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p459/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p459/r1.claim: The first two headcounts omit the conjunction before the dog's ordinal, which the author treats as evidence that they are wrong guesses.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p459/r1.anchor: ولذلك أعراه عن الواو فدل إسقاطها على أنها ليسوا ثلاثة وليس الكلب رابعا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p459/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p459/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p459/r2.claim: The phrase رجما بالغيب marks the five-person count as speculation; the seven-person count, introduced with conjunction, is presented as certain.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p459/r2.anchor: وتأخير هذا عن الرجم - وإن كان ظنا - مشعر بأنه حق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r1.claim: The conjunction can emphasize a firmly attached predicate, as in the Qur'anic phrase about every town having a known decree.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r1.anchor: فإن فائدتها توكيد لصوق الصفة بالموصوف

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r2.claim: Only a few people know the sleepers' number; this supports the prevalent seven-person view, and Ibn Abbas says he is among the few.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r2.anchor: وهو مؤيد لأنهم أصحاب القول الغالب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies himself as one of the few who know the sleepers' number.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r3.anchor: قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهمان وكان يقول : أنا من ذلك القليل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r4.claim: The Prophet should avoid disputing with people who speak without revelation, limiting discussion to the apparent evidence God revealed, and should not consult Israelite claimants.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r4.anchor: أي تجادل وتراجع { فيهم } أحدا ممن يتكلم بغير ما أخبرتك به

DURR-FULL:v5p375/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r4.speaker: اليهود
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r4.claim: Al-Suddi attributes the claim that there were three sleepers to the Jews.
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r4.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {سيقولون ثلاثة} قال: اليهود

DURR-FULL:v5p375/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r5.speaker: النصارى
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r5.claim: Al-Suddi attributes the claim that there were five sleepers to the Christians.
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r5.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {سيقولون ثلاثة} قال: اليهود {ويقولون خمسة} قال: النصارى

DURR-FULL:v5p375/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r6.claim: Throwing guesses at the unseen means making conjectures without knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {رجما بالغيب} قال: قذفا بالظن

DURR-FULL:v5p375/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r7.speaker: أبو مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r7.claim: Abu Masud says he was among the few who knew the sleepers numbered seven.
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r7.anchor: عن أبي مسعود رضي الله عنه في قوله {ما يعلمهم إلا قليل} قال: إنا من القليل كانوا سبعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r1.claim: The pronoun 'they will say' refers to contemporary People of the Torah, who disagreed about the number of sleepers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r1.anchor: الضمير في قوله سيقولون يراد به أهل التوراة، من معاصري محمد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r2.speaker: ابن محيصن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r2.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads thalath with the tāʾ assimilated into thāʾ; other readers vary the vowels of khamsa.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r3.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb means conjecture, pictured as repeatedly throwing guesses at an unknown target; the word is associated with tarjuman and the translating of a book.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r3.anchor: وقوله رجما بالغيب معناه ظنا، وهو مستعار من الرجم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r4.speaker: زهير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r4.claim: Zuhayr's line calls speech about war without direct knowledge hadithan murajjaman, a conjectural report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r4.anchor:
ومنه قول زهير: [الطويل]
وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r5.claim: The waw before 'and their eighth' is ordinary conjunction separating the final report and could be omitted; the author rejects a special 'waw of eight' rule.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r5.anchor: والواو في قوله وثامنهم طريق النحويين فيها أنها واو عطف دخلت في آخر إخبار عن عددهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r6.speaker: ابن خالويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r6.claim: Ibn Khalawayh and others call it the 'waw of eight'; al-Thaʿlabi reports Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash's claim that Quraysh inserted a waw in a sequence naming eight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r6.anchor: وتقول فرقة منها ابن خالويه: هي واو الثمانية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r7.claim: The author says examples sometimes offered for the 'waw of eight' are either wrongly analyzed or require the conjunction grammatically, as in the verses about seven nights and eight days.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r8.claim: The Prophet is told to return knowledge of their number to God; only a few among the People of the Book know, and Ibn Abbas says he is among them and that there were seven plus the dog.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r8.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول: أنا من ذلك القليل، وكانوا سبعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r9.claim: Seven is supported because the first two reported counts are explicitly called conjecture, while the seven-and-eighth report is left unchallenged; the conjunction also suits a correct count of eight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r9.anchor: بأن القرآن لما حكى قول من قال «ثلاثة وخمسة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r10.claim: One explanation of 'a manifest argument' is to rely on what revelation makes clear and return knowledge of the number to God; another is simply to tell them they are wrong without probing hidden details.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p507#2/r10.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r1.claim: The word may also mean 'departing,' supported by a poetic line; al-Tabrizi is credited with this reading at the preceding segment boundary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r1.anchor:
ظاهرا معناه ذاهبا، وأنشد:
وتلك شكاة ظاهر عنك عارها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r2.claim: The verse does not license pointless disputation: the term 'argument' is figurative for replying to People of the Book with an outward statement, unlike blameworthy hidden disputation; miraʾ derives from doubt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r2.anchor: ولم يبح له في هذه الآية أن يماري، ولكن قوله إلا مراء استعارة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r3.claim: The pronoun 'about them' refers to the sleepers, while 'from them' means the contemporary People of the Book; 'their number' is omitted but understood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p508/r3.anchor: والضمير في قوله فيهم عائد على أهل الكهف، وفي قوله منهم

JISHUMI:v6p4386/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r3.claim: Mirāʾ means disputation or argument; istiftāʾ is asking for information, and labth means residence or staying.
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r3.anchor: المراء: الجدال، ماريت الرجل أماريه مراء جادلته.

JISHUMI:v6p4386/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r4.claim: Rajman is an accusative verbal noun meaning they conjecture by conjecturing; aqrab is a comparative form that does not decline fully.
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r4.anchor: رجما نصب على المصدر أي: يرجمون رجما، كقوله: يظنون ظنا،

JISHUMI:v6p4386/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r5.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r5.claim: He explains the wāw before ‘eighth’ by treating the first phrase as a descriptive sentence and the second as a coordinated sentence; seven is a conventional peak of counting, as in 9:80.
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r5.anchor: السبعة أصل المبالغة في العدد لذلك قال: (إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة). عن علي بن عيسى.

JISHUMI:v6p4386/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r6.claim: Alī ibn ʿĪsā connects the wāw to the special rhetorical value of seven, citing the verse that commands asking forgiveness seventy times.
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r6.anchor: السبعة أصل المبالغة في العدد لذلك قال: (إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة). عن علي بن عيسى.

JISHUMI:v6p4386/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r7.claim: The wāw can mark confirmation: after reporting disputed numbers, the text confirms that the dog was the eighth, establishing seven youths.
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r7.anchor: هو واو التحقيق كأنه حكي اختلافهم ثم حكى أن ثامنهم كلبهم فهو تحقيق أنهم سبعة

JISHUMI:v6p4395/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r1.claim: The prohibition on consulting them means reports from unbelievers should not be trusted as sources of knowledge.
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r1.anchor: يوثق بقولهم لأنهم كفار. ويدل قوله

ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r2.claim: Three is nominative as predicate: disputants say the youths are three, with the dog fourth; رجما بالغيب means guesswork, as in Zuhayr's phrase الحديث المرجم.
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r2.anchor: (ثلاثة) مرفوع بخبر الابتداء، المعنى سيقول الذين يتنازعون في أمرهم؛

ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r3.claim: Adding waw in the later count but omitting it earlier has the same meaning; waw may signal that a narrative unit is complete.
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r3.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون الواو يدخل ليدل على انقطاع القصة وأن الشيء قد تم.

ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r4.speaker: زهير
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r4.claim: Zuhayr's word المرجم describes conjectural speech and witnesses رجما بالغيب.
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r4.anchor: وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتمو. . . وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم

ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Cave companions were seven and counts himself among the few who know; if authentic, this is highly reliable interpretation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال، كان أصحاب الكهف سبعة، وأنا من القليل

ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r2.claim: The Prophet should relate only the revealed apparent account and should not ask the People of the Book about the companions.
ZAJJAJ:v3p277#2/r2.anchor: أي لا تأت في أمرهم بغير ما أوحي إليك، أي أفت في قصتهم بالظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r8.speaker: السيد والعاقب
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r8.claim: The Christian visitors from Najrān report competing counts: Sayyid, a Jacobite, says three youths and a dog; al-ʿĀqib, a Nestorian, says five and a dog; Muslims say seven and a dog.
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r8.anchor: السيد والعاقب وأصحابهما من أهل نجران كانوا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r9.claim: Rāzī argues that seven plus the dog is correct: the waw before “eighth” marks a firmly established description; the first two counts are explicitly called conjecture, while this count is treated differently.
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r9.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين هذا الأخير هو الحق

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r10.claim: The waw can enter a clause describing an indefinite noun or modifying a definite noun and emphasize that the stated quality is firmly established.
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r10.anchor: هي الواو التي تدخل على الجملة الواقعة صفة

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r11.claim: Since the Qurʾān specifically adds this waw, Rāzī says it must convey an extra benefit, identifying this count as accepted rather than conjectural.
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r11.anchor: خص هذا الموضع بهذا الحرف الزائد

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r12.claim: Calling the first two counts “conjecture” implies that the remaining count differs from them and is not baseless guessing.
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r12.anchor: وتخصيص الشيء بالوصف يدل على أن الحال

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r13.claim: The following statement that only a few know their number distinguishes the seven-count from the first two guesses and implies its greater accuracy.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r14.claim: ʿAlī says the seven were Yamlikhā, Maksalmīnā, Maslathīnā, Marnūs, Dabarnūs, Sādanūs, and the shepherd, and names the dog Quṭmīr.
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r14.anchor: كان علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه يقول

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says he is one of the few who know their number and affirms that they were seven and their dog was the eighth.
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r15.anchor: وكان ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما يقول

RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r1.claim: Rāzī's sixth argument is that God likely included the true count among the three reported counts; since the first two are conjecture, the third must be correct.
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r1.anchor: فثبت أن جملة الأقوال الحقة والباطلة

RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r2.claim: His seventh argument is that the Prophet was told not to dispute or consult them and that only a few know; the Prophet must have learned the correct count from revelation. The arguments together yield strength despite unequal force.
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r2.anchor: فعلمنا أن العلم بهذه الواقعة حصل للنبي عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r3.claim: The phrase “they will say” omits “they” because the subject is clear from context.

RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r4.claim: The future particle appears before the first opinion, while conjunction carries the following two opinions into its scope.
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r4.anchor: أن حرف العطف يوجب دخول القولين الآخرين فيه

RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r5.claim: Rajm is throwing and ghayb is what is unseen; “guessing at the unseen” means speaking about what one does not truly know, without reflection.
RAZI-FULL:v21p90/r5.anchor: معناه أن يرى ما غاب عنه ولا يعرفه بالحقيقة

RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r1.claim: A proposed “wāw of eight” says Arabs use seven for numerical abundance and mark the eighth with a waw of resumption; al-Qaffāl objects that the eighth descriptor in 59:23 has no waw.
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r1.anchor: والناس يسمون هذه الواو واو الثمانية

RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r2.claim: Only God, or those He informs, knows the detailed events of past and future; Ibn ʿAbbās claims to be one of the few, while al-Qāḍī says that claim is sound only if the Prophet informed him. Rāzī finds the combined evidence probabilistic, not conclusive.
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r2.anchor: العلم بتفاصيل كائنات العالم والحوادث التي حدثت

RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r3.claim: Do not argue over the precise count: say there is no evidence for their count and suspend judgment; the verse parallels the command to debate People of the Book graciously.
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r3.anchor: أن لا يكذبهم في تعيين ذلك العدد

RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r4.claim: Because the other disputants lack knowledge, the Prophet is also told not to ask them about the sleepers.
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r4.anchor: ليس عندهم علم في هذا الباب

RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p91/r5.claim: Opponents of analogical reasoning cite “guessing at the unseen” as proof that conjecture is blameworthy and that issuing a legal opinion based on conjecture is forbidden; a line glossed by al-Kashshāf uses rajm for what is merely supposed.

RAZI-FULL:v21p92/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p92/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p92/r1.claim: Al-Kashshāf's cited line “it is not a report about her that is conjectured” uses marjum to mean supposed or conjectured.
RAZI-FULL:v21p92/r1.anchor: أي المظنون هكذا قاله صاحب الكشاف

TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r1.claim: The first two reported counts, three and five, are conjecture; the uncondemned third count implies seven, also supported by the earlier dialogue suggesting at least seven youths.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r1.anchor: وقد ذكره الله سبحانه ولم يعقبه بشيء يدل على تزييفه

TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r2.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb describes both rejected counts as unsupported speech; rajm evokes throwing stones blindly at an unknown target, while a gloss as mere conjecture is less apt.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r2.anchor: وهذا التوصيف راجع إلى القولين جميعا ولو اختص بالثاني فقط كان من حق الكلام أن يقدم القول الثاني

TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses the numbers as predicates with omitted subjects and the dog clauses as adjectives; he explains the waw as joining a clause adjectivally and making the attribution emphatic and settled.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r3.anchor: قال في الكشاف وثلاثة خبر مبتدأ محذوف

TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r4.claim: The description rajman bil-ghayb grammatically characterizes both the three and five counts, since restricting it to the five count would require a different order of presentation.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#19/r4.anchor: وهذا التوصيف راجع إلى القولين جميعا ولو اختص بالثاني فقط

TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to say that when the waw appears, the count ends: seven youths and their dog is definite and certain.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس حين وقعت الواو انقطعت العدة أي لم يبق بعدها عدة عاد يلتفت إليها

TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r2.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r2.claim: The Majmaʿ account rejects the proposed waw of eight, saying grammarians do not recognize it; the alleged eight gates of Paradise do not establish such a rule.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r2.anchor: وقال في المجمع في ذيل ما لخص به كلام أبي علي الفارسي وأما من قال هذه الواو واو الثمانية

TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r3.claim: God's instruction to defer knowledge of their count to Him parallels the youths’ response about duration; the wording implies a few people, likely People of the Book, did know it.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r3.anchor: يفيد نفي الحال فالاستثناء منه بقوله

TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r4.claim: The three counts were established opinions in the Prophet’s time; the future forms may indicate their near-future circulation relative to revelation or the event.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r4.anchor: مفاد الكلام أن الأقوال الثلاثة كانت محققة في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r5.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r5.claim: Al-Raghib defines mirya as hesitation, more specific than doubt, and mumara as disputation over an uncertain matter; he links the root to rubbing a camel’s udder for milk.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r5.anchor: قال الراغب المرية التردد في الأمر وهو أخص من الشك

TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r6.claim: A manifest dispute means not probing beyond the Quran’s account and neither insulting nor refuting the other side; another gloss takes it as argument that defeats an opponent.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#20/r6.anchor: والمراد بكون المراء ظاهرا أن لا يتعمق فيه بالاقتصار على ما قصه القرآن

TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r1.claim: The author cites a line using zahir for a complaint whose blemish has disappeared from the addressee, supporting the alternative sense that a manifest argument has removed the opponent’s case.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r2.claim: Because God has told the Prophet the youths’ account, he should debate only briefly from that account and not seek further rulings from the People of the Book.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r2.anchor: فلا تحاجهم في الفتية إلا محاجة ظاهرة

TABRISI:18:21-24/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-24/r4.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:18:21-24/r4.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā says the first two number clauses describe the preceding indefinite number, while ‘and their eighth was their dog’ coordinates a sentence with another sentence; seven is a base number of emphasis.
TABRISI:18:21-24/r4.anchor: لأن ها هنا عطف جملة على جملة وهناك وصف النكرة بجملة فإن التقدير هم سبعة وهم ثلاثة

TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r1.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r1.claim: An explanatory clause can follow what it explains without a conjunction.
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r1.anchor: وأما الثالث: وهي الجملة التي تكون تفسيرا لما قبلها

TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r2.claim: A clause linked by a shared referent may connect to what precedes either with or without a conjunction.
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r2.anchor: فإن هذا الوجه يتصل بما قبله على وجهين أحدهما: بحرف عطف

TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r5.claim: ‘And their eighth was their dog’ is not a circumstantial clause, description, explanation, or wholly separate statement: the reported number is disputed, and the added wāw marks a link that shared reference alone does not supply.
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r5.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون تفسيرا لأن التفسير هو المفسر في المعنى ولا يجوز أن يكون شيء من جزء الجملة

TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r6.claim: The final clause cannot modify the past participle as an adjective: a past participle does not operate as a present verb, and the sentence is independent rather than a descriptive clause.
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r6.anchor: ولا يجوز الأول لأنه في معنى الماضي والماضي لا يقدر فيه الانفصال

TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r7.claim: The wāw can be omitted from ‘their eighth is their dog’ because the clause itself mentions the people named before and thereby already signals the connection.
TABRISI:18:21-24#2/r7.anchor: فحذفت الواو واستغني عنها إذا كانت إنما تذكر لتدل على الاتصال وما في الجملة من ذكر ما في الأولى

TABRISI:18:21-22/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:21-22/r1.claim: An alternative account places the dispute after the ruler and people entered the cave and the youths fell dead; some proposed a tomb-like building, others a mosque at the entrance.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r1.anchor: وهذا التنازع كان منهم بعد العلم بموتهم عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:18:21-22/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r2.speaker: مشركو ذلك الوقت
TABRISI:18:21-22/r2.claim: The command to build a structure is attributed to the polytheists of that time, who proposed concealing the youths from public view behind it.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r2.anchor: أي قال مشركو ذلك الوقت { ابنوا عليهم بنيانا }

TABRISI:18:21-22/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-22/r3.claim: ‘Their Lord knows best’ can mean that God knows their condition in the disagreement over what should be done with them.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r3.anchor: ربهم أعلم بحالهم فيما تنازعوا فيه

TABRISI:18:21-22/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-22/r4.claim: Another gloss takes ‘their Lord knows best’ as acknowledging that their Creator, who put them to sleep and raised them, knows their state and how their case stands.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r4.anchor: خالقهم الذي أنامهم وبعثهم أعلم بحالهم

TABRISI:18:21-22/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-22/r5.claim: A further gloss says the people were unsure whether the youths remained sleeping and alive or had died; some said they had died, while others said they would not die until the Resurrection.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r5.anchor: أأحياء نيام هم أم أموات فقد قيل إنهم ماتوا

TABRISI:18:21-22/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:18:21-22/r6.claim: Those who prevailed over the affair are variously identified as the believing ruler and his companions, the believing guardians of the cave youths, or the town's leaders.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r6.anchor: رؤساء البلد الذين استولوا على أمرهم عن الجبائي

TABRISI:18:21-22/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-22/r7.claim: The mosque is a place of worship, and the proposal indicates that believers had prevailed in the town; al-Hasan alternatively says it was where the youths would pray if they awoke.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r7.anchor: ودل ذلك على أن الغلبة كانت للمؤمنين

TABRISI:18:21-22/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:18:21-22/r8.claim: An alternative explanation is that the mosque was made so the cave youths could pray there if they awoke.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r8.anchor: يصلي فيه أصحاب الكهف إذا استيقظوا عن الحسن

TABRISI:18:21-22/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-22/r9.claim: A report says the youths asked God to restore their former state after learning how long they had slept; God restored it and diverted seekers by making them lose the way to the cave.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r9.anchor: سألوا الله تعالى أن يعيدهم إلى حالتهم الأولى فأعادهم إليها

TABRISI:18:21-22/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r10.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:18:21-22/r10.claim: The claim that three or five youths had the dog as fourth or sixth is conjecture without certainty.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r10.anchor: أي قذفا بالظن من غير يقين عن قتادة

TABRISI:18:21-22/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-22/r11.claim: When Christians from Najran visited the Prophet, Jacobites said three and Nestorians five, while Muslims said seven youths with the dog as the eighth.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r11.anchor: فقالت اليعقوبية منهم: كانوا ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم

TABRISI:18:21-22/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r12.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:18:21-22/r12.claim: Only a few people know the youths' number; another report specifies that the few are people of scripture.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r12.anchor: ما يعلمهم إلا قليل } من الناس عن قتادة

TABRISI:18:21-22/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:21-22/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says the youths were seven and their dog was eighth, and the author says the likeliest source of his knowledge was the Prophet.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r13.anchor: أنا من ذلك القليل هم سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم

TABRISI:18:21-22/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r14.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:18:21-22/r14.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits Ibn Abbas's list of the seven youths by name: Maksalimina, Tamlīkha, Martūlus, Nīnūnus, Sārīnūnus, Darbūnus, and Kashūṭbūnus; the eighth was the shepherd.
TABRISI:18:21-22/r14.anchor: هم مكسليمنا وتمليخا ومرطولس ونينونس وسارينونس

TABRISI:18:22-24/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:22-24/r1.claim: One interpretation of ‘do not dispute’ allows only debate grounded in the revealed account and proof; Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Mujahid are named for this view.
TABRISI:18:22-24/r1.anchor: إلا بما أظهرنا لك من أمرهم عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد

TABRISI:18:22-24/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:22-24/r2.claim: A second interpretation permits a public argument that points out conflicting counts and asks the opponents to bring proof, since either claim could be true or false.
TABRISI:18:22-24/r2.anchor: أثبتم عددا وخالفكم غيركم وكلا القولين يحتمل الصدق والكذب

TABRISI:18:22-24/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:22-24/r3.claim: A third interpretation says debate should occur before witnesses so opponents cannot later claim secret prior knowledge and mislead weaker people.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:22-24/r4.claim: The Prophet is told not to seek information about the youths or their number from scripture scholars; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada are cited.
TABRISI:18:22-24/r4.anchor: ولا تستفتهم من جهتهم عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:18:22-24/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:22-24/r5.claim: Although addressed to the Prophet, the prohibition is meant for others, since he trusted God's report and should not turn to questioning Jews.
TABRISI:18:22-24/r5.anchor: والخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد غيره

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r2.claim: The coming statements about the sleepers are attributed to the People of the Book.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r3.claim: Qatāda says the guesses of three or five sleepers are speculation about the unseen; al-Suddī calls them claims based on conjecture.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: أي قذفا بالغيب. وقال السدي: رميا بقول الظن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r4.claim: Qatāda says only a few people know the number; Ibn ʿAbbās said he was among the few and that they were seven, with the dog eighth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r4.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: إلا قليل من الناس.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r5.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says to debate the People of the Book only with what God has revealed; Qatāda says the account already given is sufficient.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r5.anchor: قال: {فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا} [الكهف: 22] يقول الله للنبي: فلا تمار أهل الكتاب في أصحاب الكهف {إلا مراء ظاهرا} [الكهف: 22] إلا بما أخبرتك في تفسير الحسن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is told not to ask any Jew about the sleepers; Jews had questioned him in order to trap him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r1.anchor: {ولا تستفت فيهم} [الكهف: 22] في أصحاب الكهف. {منهم أحدا} [الكهف: 22] من اليهود. يقول: لا تسل عنهم من اليهود أحدا.

ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r1.claim: Most people speculate about the unseen, so Elmalılı advises limiting discussion to a superficial debate rather than prolonged disputation.
ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r1.anchor: bilenler azdır, çoğu gayb taşlıyorlar. Onun için zâhirî bir münakaşadan başka bir mücadele ve mübahaseye dalma

ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r2.claim: Knowing the companions' exact number is unnecessary to the lesson, and only a few know it; most people speculate about the unseen.
ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r2.anchor: Adedlerinin bilinmesi kıssa nokta-i nazarından herkese lâzım değildir

ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r3.claim: The Prophet should avoid prolonged argument about the sleepers and should not ask any of the competing claimants; the Quran already explains what needs to be known.
ELMALILI:18:19-22#2/r3.anchor: Şu hâlde Ashâb-ı Kehf kıssasını yalnız Kur’ân’ın beyânına dikkat ederek okumalı, şundan bundan sormaya kalkışmamalıdır

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The verse is a parenthetical instruction to the Prophet: when people try to draw him into disputes over the cave-dwellers, he should offer only a brief diversion and ask no details beyond the Qur'an's account.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This is a parenthetical sentence addresed to the Prophet (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Mumarat means debate and argument; people addicted to polemics keep shifting issues rather than seeking truth, so a wise person should politely leave them alone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: people who are inflicted with the ailment of polemical debate and argument have no interest in the truth itself

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Some exegetes read the unchallenged third estimate, seven youths and a dog as the eighth, as the Qur'an's verdict; Islahi says this reading seems correct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This opinion seems to be the correct one but my own opinion in this regard

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Despite that reading, Islahi's own position follows the Qur'an's stated reserve: only God knows their number, and few people know it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: only my Lord knows better their number; few people know them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The parenthetical discussion in verses 22–24 ends here; this statement returns to the earlier estimates of the cave-dwellers' number.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The parenthetical sentence that began with verse 22 ended on verse 24

BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r1.claim: The three reports belong to disputants in the Prophet's era among scripturalists and Muslims, but the source does not assign every statement to every group.
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r1.anchor: للخائضين في قصتهم في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أهل الكتاب والمسلمين

BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r2.speaker: اليهود
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r2.claim: The Jews say the sleepers were three, with the dog making a fourth.
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r2.anchor: أي : سيقول اليهود هم أي : أصحاب الكهف

BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r3.speaker: النصارى
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r3.claim: The Christians say five sleepers and a sixth dog, but this is conjecture about the unseen; rajman can be circumstantial or a cognate accusative.
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r3.anchor: أي : النصارى وإنما لم يجىء بالسين اكتفاء بعطفه

BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r4.speaker: المسلمون
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r4.claim: The Muslims say seven sleepers and their dog as a conclusion received through revelation, not a conjecture like the preceding claims.
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r4.anchor: القائلون المسلمون بطرق التلقن من هذا الوحي

BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r5.claim: The added waw in the seven-count formulation and its distinct wording convey a firmer relation and show it is guided by revelation rather than guesswork.
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r5.anchor: وتغيير سبكه بزيادة الواو المفيدة لزيادة وكادة النسبة

BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r6.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r6.claim: My Lord knows best means stronger and more complete knowledge, since certainty has degrees; the comparison is not with the first two groups, who have no share in knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p179#2/r6.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي أي : أقوى علما وأزيد في الكيفية

BURSEVI:v5p180/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p180/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p180/r1.claim: Only a few know the sleepers' number, having been guided to use the relevant indications as evidence.
BURSEVI:v5p180/r1.anchor: ما يعلمهم عدتهم إلا قليل من الناس قد وفقهم الله للاستشهاد بتلك الشواهد

BURSEVI:v5p180/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p180/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p180/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the waw as closing the count: there is no further number after seven, and the dog is eighth.
BURSEVI:v5p180/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما حين وقعت الواو وانقطعت العدة

BURSEVI:v5p180/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p180/r3.speaker: علي
BURSEVI:v5p180/r3.claim: Ali names six companions of the king and a seventh shepherd who joined their flight; the shepherd's name has variant forms.
BURSEVI:v5p180/r3.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنهم سبعة نفر أسماؤهم يمليخا ومكشليينا

BURSEVI:v5p180/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p180/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p180/r4.claim: Al-Kashifi says the shepherd's name is more correctly Martush.

BURSEVI:v5p180/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p180/r5.speaker: النيسابوري عن ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p180/r5.claim: A report attributed through Ibn Abbas recommends writing the sleepers' names for protection, healing, safe travel, childbirth, crops, wealth, and access to rulers.
BURSEVI:v5p180/r5.anchor: قال النيسابوري عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن أسماء أصحاب الكهف تصلح للطلب والهرب

BURSEVI:v5p180/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p180/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p180/r6.claim: Since the first two counts are ignorant, avoid deep dispute; state the Quranic account without humiliating them and do not consult people who lack knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p180/r6.anchor: إذ قد عرفت جهل أصحاب القولين الأولين فلا تجادلهم

BURSEVI:v5p180/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p180/r7.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p180/r7.claim: One esoteric interpretation makes the seven sleepers the seven abdal sustaining the world's seven climes, their cave a retreat, and their dog the animal soul.
BURSEVI:v5p180/r7.anchor: بعض كويند اين قصه نمود از أحوال بدلاء سبعة است

ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya and other scholars take the pronouns in the three predictions to refer to contemporary Jews disputing the cave story; al-Alusi notes that this implies some Torah knowledge but is not convincing to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r1.anchor: الضمير فيه وفي الفعلين بعد كما اختاره ابن عطية وبعض المحققين لليهود المعاصرين له

ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r2.claim: The future tense predicts what they will say when Muhammad tells the story or they are asked for the youths' number.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا إخبار بما لم يكن واقعا بعد كأنه قيل سيقولون إذا قصصت قصة أصحاب الكهف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r3.claim: The first claim means three persons, with the dog making the fourth; the omitted predicate is 'are', and the following clause describes the group.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r3.anchor: رابعهم ( أي جاعلهم أربعة بانضمامه إليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r4.claim: Al-Tibi's parsing makes the clause an adjective to 'three'; its wording gives the youths a special distinction and rhetorically joins even their dog to their blessed company.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r4.anchor: وإلى هذا الإعراب ذهب أبو البقاء واختاره العلامة الطيبي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r5.claim: The numeral should be understood as three persons, not three men, since counting three men plus a dog as four would mix categories contrary to common usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p240#2/r5.anchor: وتقدير تمييز العدد أشخاص أولى من تقديره رجال لأنه تصير الثلاثة الرجال أربعة بكلبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r1.speaker: ابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r1.claim: Ibn Muhaysin assimilates the final thāʾ of thalāthatun into the following tāʾ because the sounds are close in articulation and both voiceless.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن ( ثلاثة ) بإدغام الثاء في التاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r2.claim: The five-sixth claim is also future; conjunction to sayūqūlūna places it under the same future sense, though taking it as a fresh present is a strained analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r2.anchor: عطف على ( سيقولون ) والمضارع وإن كان مشتركا بين الحال والاستقبال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r3.speaker: شبل بن عباد عن ابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r3.claim: Shibl ibn Abbad transmits a reading of khamsata with fatḥa on the mīm, a dialectal form alongside the still pronunciation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r3.anchor: وقرأ شبل بن عباد عن ابن كثير ( خمسة ) بفتح الميم وهو كالسكون

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r4.speaker: ابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r4.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads khamsa with kasra on khāʾ and mīm, assimilating tāʾ into sīn; another transmission assimilates tanwīn into sīn without nasalization.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن بكسر الخاء والميم وبإدغام التاء في السين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r5.claim: Rajman bi-l-ghayb means speaking of hidden matters without access to them, either as a blind throw or as unsupported conjecture.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r5.anchor: أي رميا بالخبر الغائب الخفي عنهم الذي لا مطلع لهم عليه وإتيانا به أو ظنا بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r6.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r6.claim: Al-Kashf explains the metaphor as words about an unknown matter thrown without aiming at a known target, unlike a deliberate and reliable shot.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r6.anchor: جعل الكلام الغائب عنهم علمه بمنزلة الرجام المرمى به لا يقصد به مخاطب معين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r7.claim: The metaphor can also become an idiom for conjecture, since rajman bi-l-ẓann was commonly used to mean supposing without certainty.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r7.anchor: وفي الكشف أيضا أنه لما كثر استعمال قولهم : رجما بالظن فهموا من المصدر معناه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r8.speaker: زهير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r8.claim: Zuhayr's verse uses al-ḥadīth al-murajjam to mean conjectural speech, illustrating the idiomatic sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r8.anchor: قول زهير : وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتموا وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r9.claim: Rajman may be circumstantial or a verbal noun attached to the act of speaking; Abu Hayyan also allows it to be a purpose phrase, an analysis al-Alusi deems weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r9.anchor: وانتصاب ( رجما ) هنا على الوجهين إما على الحالية من الضمير في الفعلين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r10.claim: The suggestion that the dog was elevated to rational beings by their company is poetic fantasy.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241/r10.anchor: والقول بأن الكلب بشرف صحبتهم ألحق بالعقلاء تخيل شعري

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the clause 'and their dog is the eighth' as an adjective linked to seven by an added waw; he says the waw marks a firmly attached, settled attribute, so this is the true count, unlike the two guesses labeled conjecture.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r1.anchor: وهي التي أذنت هنا بأن قائلي ما ذكر قالوه عن ثبات علم وطمأنينة نفس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when the waw appeared, the count ended: the youths were certainly seven, with the dog eighth.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r2.anchor: يدل كلام ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما فقد روي أنه قال : حين وقعت الواو

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r3.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r3.claim: Ata says the few who know the number are from the People of the Book; another view takes them to be few among all humanity.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r3.anchor: وقد نص عطاء على أن هذا القليل من أهل الكتاب وقيل من البشر مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r4.claim: A sound-chain report in al-Tabarani's al-Awsaṭ has Ibn Abbas say he is one of the few who know the number; a similar report comes from Ibn Masud.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p241#2/r4.anchor: أنا من أولئك القليل وأخرجه عنه غير واحد من طرق شتى وأخرج نحوه ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r1.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r1.claim: Ibn al-Munir supports al-Zamakhshari's account of the waw and rejects the so-called waw of eight as an unstable grammatical claim.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r1.anchor: وإلى كون الواو كما ذكر الزمخشري ذهب ابن المنير وقال بعد نقله : وهو الصواب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa says a clause serving as an adjective to an indefinite noun may take a waw, which he applies to thāminuhum.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : الجملة إذا وقعت صفة للنكرة جاز أن يدخلها الواو

ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the claim that waw marks a clause attached as an adjective, arguing that grammarians do not recognize this function and that the cited Qur'anic clause is circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r3.anchor: كون الواو تدخل على الجملة الواقعة صفة دالة على لصوق الصفة بالموصوف وعلى ثبوت اتصاله بها شيء لا يعرفه النحويون

ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r4.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r4.claim: The author of al-Farāʾid argues that a waw between adjective and noun is incoherent: they are one in essence and judgment, while conjunction implies two things and does not itself confirm attachment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r4.anchor: دخول الواو بين الصفة والموصوف غير مستقيم لاتحاد الصفة والموصوف ذاتا وحكما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r5.speaker: صاحب المفتاح
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r5.claim: The author of al-Miftāḥ calls it a mistake to treat the waw in 'a town except it had a known decree' as connecting adjective and noun; he parses it as circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r5.anchor: ذكر صاحب المفتاح أن قول من قال : إن الواو في قوله تعالى ( ولها كتاب معلوم ) داخلة بين الصفة والموصوف سهو منه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan also rejects the proposed adjective parsing of 'a man came with another' and distinguishes it from a circumstantial clause following a known noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p242/r6.anchor: وأما جاءني رجل ومعه آخر ففيه وجهان أحدهما أن يكون جملتين متعاطفتين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r1.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r1.claim: Al-Tibi defends al-Zamakhshari by treating the waw as metaphorical rather than literally conjunctive; metaphor may occur in particles, and waw and bāʾ share a sense of combination or attachment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r1.anchor: فالواو هنا ليست على الحقيقة و لايعتبر في المجاز النقل الخصوصي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r2.claim: A report from Sibawayh treats the waw in 'I sold the sheep and a dirham' as meaning bāʾ, since conjunction and attachment share a relation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r2.anchor: نقل شارح اللباب عن سيبويه أن الواو في قولهم : بعت الشاة ودرهما بمعنى الباء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r3.claim: Al-Tibi says the metaphorical waw emphasizes the adjective's attachment to its noun and signals that the quality is inseparable; circumstantial clauses are adjectives by another consideration.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r3.anchor: أن للصفة نوع اتصال بالموصوف فإذا أريد توكيد اللصوق وسط بينهما الواو

ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r4.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r4.claim: Ibn al-Hajib says the clauses describing fourth and sixth cannot be adjectives or circumstances without a governing element, and may instead be successive predicates for an omitted subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r4.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون ( رابعهم كلبهم وسادسهم كلبهم ) صفة لما قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r5.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r5.claim: He also suggests that the eighth-dog clause could be a divine insertion rather than a report by the speakers, which would validate the count; al-Alusi rejects this as a reading worth adopting.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r5.anchor: أما إذا قيل إن قوله تعالى ( وثامنهم كلبهم ) استئناف منه سبحانه لا حكاية عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r6.claim: Al-Alusi says the objection that divine confirmation would make too many people know the count is weak: 'few' is relative, need not mean fewer than ten, and could refer to those who knew before confirmation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r6.anchor: ولا اختصاص للقليل بما دون العشرة وإن أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن وهب بن منبه أنه قال : كل قليل في القرآن فهو دون العشرة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r7.claim: He favors taking the final clause as evidence that the third claim is true: the first two are explicitly conjecture, and the few who know can include a small group of Muslims or People of the Book.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r7.anchor: لأنه قد اندفع به القولان الأولان فيكون الصادق هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r8.claim: The eloquent passage need not flatten differing reports into one grammatical form; their distinct wording can carry distinct benefits and preserve the passage's rhetorical force.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r8.anchor: لأن في كل اختلاف فوائد والبليغ من ينظر إلى تلك الفوائد لا من يرده إلى التطويل والحشو

ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r9.speaker: السيد المحقق
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r9.claim: A leading verifier supports al-Zamakhshari: the eighth-dog clause is an adjective to seven, as its parallels show, and waw metaphorically reinforces attachment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r9.anchor: وافق في الانتصار جماعة منهم سيد المحققين وسند المدققين فقال : الظاهر أن قوله تعالى ( وثامنهم كلبهم ) صفة لسبعة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r10.speaker: السكاكي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r10.claim: Al-Sakkaki says waw as a conjunction signals difference; the defense of adjective-linking therefore treats it metaphorically as a relation marker.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p243/r10.anchor: على أن الواو عاطفة لأنها هي التي تقتضي المغايرة كما قال السكاكي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r1.claim: A circumstantial clause can follow an indefinite noun for reasons beyond the noun already being described, including the presence of a waw; this answers one objection to the adjective analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r1.anchor: لا ينحصر مسوغ مجيء الحال من النكرة في كونها موصوفة أو في حكم الموصوفة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r2.speaker: ابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r2.claim: Ibn Malik rejects al-Zamakhshari's analysis in five ways: adjective differs from circumstance, the view lacks grammatical precedent, waw signals difference, separates rather than joins, and should occur where a circumstance is impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r2.anchor: ما ذهب إليه صاحب الكشاف من توسط الواو بين الصفة والموصوف فاسد من خمسة أوجه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r3.speaker: ابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r3.claim: His first objection is that circumstances may precede their nouns, differ in inflection, definiteness, and number, and may omit a pronoun with waw, unlike adjectival clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p244/r3.anchor: لجواز تقدم الحال على صاحبها وجواز تخالفهما في الإعراب والتعريف والتنكير

ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r1.claim: Al-Alusi calls Ibn Malik's fourth objection—that waw separates what should be attached—an astonishing error even children would recognize.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r1.anchor: والعجب مما ذكره في الوجه الرابع فهو توهم يستغرب من الأطفال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r2.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r2.claim: One account assigns the first count to Jews and the second to Christians; the third is attributed to some Muslims, with the Qur'anic wording said to have guided them to the truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r2.anchor: فالقول الأول لليهود على ما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن السدي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r3.claim: An alternative assigns the first count to a Jacobite delegation from Najran and the second to Nestorian Christians led by al-ʿAqib; the third belongs to Muslims, whom the verse guides toward the truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r3.anchor: وقيل لسيد من سادات نصارى العرب النجرانيين وكان يعقوبيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r4.claim: Some say the Prophet learned the true count through separate revelation; critics ask why Ibn Abbas knew it while most companions did not, and the reply is that the Prophet may have told only a few.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r4.anchor: وقيل إنهم علموا تلك العدة من وحي غير ما ذكر بأن يكون قد أخبرهم صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r5.claim: Another objection says eloquent Arab companions should have perceived the Qur'anic clues as well as later commentators; the proposed reply is that few heard this Meccan verse or attended to its clues.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r5.anchor: بل لأنهم العرب الذين أرضعوا ثدى البلاغة في مهد الفصاحة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r6.claim: The explanation that only a few heard the verse in Mecca or noticed its indications is possible but, in al-Alusi's view, unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p245/r6.anchor: ولا يكاد يدفع هذا الايراد إلا بالتزام أن السامعين لهذه الآية قليلون لأنها نزلت في مكة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r1.speaker: الماوردي وأبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r1.claim: Al-Mawardi, followed by Abu Hayyan, says the pronouns refer to people who disputed the count before the youths were discovered; al-Alusi finds this unlikely because the verse uses future tense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r1.anchor: وقال الماوردي واستظهره أبو حيان : إن الضمائر للمتنازعين في حديثهم قبل ظهورهم عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r2.claim: Another possibility is that the pronouns refer to groups who discovered the cave but could not see its occupants; the final group may have asked the returning youth, believed his count, and spoken from inherited reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r2.anchor: إن الضمائر للمعثرين اختلفوا في عددهم لعدم تمكنهم من رؤيتهم والاجتماع معهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r3.claim: Al-Alusi dismisses the strange claim that the pronoun in 'they say seven' refers to God using the majestic plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r3.anchor: ومن غريب ما قيل : إن الضمير في ( يقولون سبعة ) لله عز وجل والجمع للتعظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r4.claim: One report gives the youths' names as Miksalmina, Yamlikha, Martulus, Thabiyunus, Dardunus, Kafashṭaṭiyus, and Manṭunawasis, the shepherd; their dog was Qiṭmīr.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r4.anchor: أسماؤهم على ما صح عن ابن عباس مكسلمينا ويمليخا ومرطولس وثبيونس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r5.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r5.claim: A report attributed to Ali gives another set of names and says six were advisers to the king while the seventh was a shepherd; al-Alusi questions whether the report is reliably attributed to Ali.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r5.anchor: وروي عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أن أسمائهم يمليخا ومكشلينيا ومثلينيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r6.claim: The transmitted spellings of the youths' foreign names vary too much to inspire confidence; Ibn Hajar and al-Baḥr both note instability or weak transmission.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r6.anchor: وذكر الحافظ ابن حجر في شرح البخاري أن في النطق بأسمائهم اختلافا كثيرا ولا يقع الوثوق

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r7.claim: Al-Naysaburi attributes to Ibn Abbas claims that writing the youths' names protects from fire, illness, childbirth danger, poverty, rulers, sea travel, and killing; al-Alusi says these claims are unfounded fabrications used to take money.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r7.anchor: إن أسماء أصحاب الكهف تصلح للطلب والهرب وإطفاء الحريق تكتب في خرقة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r8.claim: Al-Alusi sarcastically says that taking money from credulous women may itself be the names' one proven property.
