ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r8.anchor: ولعله شيء افتراه المتزيون بزي المشايخ لأخذ الدراهم من النساء وسخفة العقول

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r9.claim: A noncanonical reading has kālbihim, 'their herder'; some use it to infer eight men, while the standard reading is explained by supplying 'companion/owner' of their dog.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r9.anchor: وقريء ( وثامنهم كالبهم ) أي صاحب كلبهم + واستدل بعضهم بهذه القراءة على أنهم ثمانية رجال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r10.claim: Since one report is right and the others mistaken, do not argue deeply about the youths; limit discussion to revelation and avoid humiliating those who are wrong.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r10.anchor: إذا قد وقفت على أن في الخائضين مخطئا ومصيبا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r11.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r11.claim: Al-Raghib defines murāʾ as disputation about something doubtful, deriving the word from rubbing a she-camel's udder to milk it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r11.anchor: والمماراة على ما قال الراغب المحاجة فيما فيه مرية أي تردد وأصل ذلك من مريت الناقة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says apparent argument means telling the disputants, 'It is not as you know'.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p246/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : المراء الظاهر القول لهم ليس كما تعلمون

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r1.speaker: الماوردي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r1.claim: Al-Mawardi defines apparent argument as one supported by clear proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r1.anchor: وحكى الماوردي أن المراء الظاهر ما كان بحجة ظاهرة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says it is the argument of a scholar certain of the report's truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري : هو جدال العالم المتيقن بحقيقة الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r3.speaker: ابن بحر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r3.claim: Ibn Baḥr says apparent argument is what people can witness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r3.anchor: وقال ابن بحر : هو ما يشهده الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r4.speaker: التبريزي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r4.claim: Al-Tabrizi takes apparent argument as one that defeats the opponent, citing a poem where ẓāhir means gone.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r4.anchor: وقال التبريزي : المراد من الظاهر الذاهب بحجة الخصم يقال ظهر إذا ذهب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r5.claim: Do not ask the disputants for a ruling or information about the youths, since revelation suffices and they lack knowledge; this also avoids unnecessary appeasement or discourtesy.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r5.anchor: فإن فيما أفتيناك غني عن الاستفتاء فيحمل على التفتي المنافي لمكارم الأخلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r6.claim: Another interpretation says not to accept the third count merely because some disputant said it, but to accept it only because revelation supplied it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r6.anchor: وقيل : المعنى لا ترجع إليهم في شأن الفتية ولا تصدق القول الثالث من حيث صدوره منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r7.claim: A further view says not to consult either mistaken faction because they are ignorant, but al-Alusi calls this reading contrary to the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247/r7.anchor: وهو خلاف الظاهر كما لا يخفى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r1.speaker: السيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r1.claim: In the account of the Christian visitors from Najran, al-Sayyid, a Jacobite, says the cave companions were three, with their dog fourth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r1.anchor: فقال السيد -وكان يعقوبيا-: كانوا ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r2.speaker: العاقب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r2.claim: In the same report, al-Aqib, a Nestorian, says they were five, with their dog sixth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r2.anchor: وقال العاقب -وكان نسطوريا-: كانوا خمسة سادسهم كلبهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r3.speaker: المسلمون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r3.claim: The Muslims say they were seven, with their dog eighth; the passage's contrast presents this as the confirmed claim.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r3.anchor: وقال المسلمون: كانوا سبعة ثامنهم كلبهم فحقق الله قول المسلمين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r4.claim: The first two claims are called guesses about the unseen, while the seven-and-dog claim is not so labeled.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r4.anchor: رجما بالغيب} (2) أي: ظنا وحدسا من غير يقين ولم يقل هذا في حق السبعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r5.claim: One view says there is no difference in meaning whether the conjunction before eighth is omitted or included.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r5.anchor: اختلفوا في الواو في قوله: {وثامنهم} قيل: تركها وذكرها سواء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r6.claim: Another view calls it the waw of judgment and confirmation: after reporting the disagreement, the text confirms the seven by saying their dog was eighth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: هي واو الحكم والتحقيق كأنه حكى اختلافهم وتم الكلام عند قوله ويقولون سبعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r7.claim: A third view calls it the waw of eight, claiming Arabs counted one through seven and then said and eight because seven completed their number cycle.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: هذه واو الثمانية وذلك أن العرب تعد فتقول واحد اثنان ثلاثة أربعة خمسة ستة سبعة وثمانية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r8.claim: The proposed waw of eight is compared with the lists in 9:112 and 66:5.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161#2/r8.anchor: نظيره قوله تعالى (3) "التائبون العابدون الحامدون" إلى قوله: "والناهون عن المنكر"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says he is among the few who know their number and that they were seven.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أنا من القليل كانوا سبعة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says there were eight and reads the wording as saying their dog was their guardian; the author says the seven is correct.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: كانوا ثمانية قرأ: {وثامنهم كلبهم} أي: حافظهم والصحيح هو الأول.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas also gives the seven companions' names—Maksalmina, Yamlikha, Martunus, Baynunus, Sarinunus, Dhu Nuwanas, and Kashfitattunus—plus their shepherd and dog Qitmir.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: هم مكسلمينا ويمليخا ومرطونس وبينونس وسارينونس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r4.claim: Do not argue beyond the apparent account or add details; what has been told is sufficient.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r4.anchor: {فلا تمار فيهم} أي: لا تجادل ولا تقل في عددهم وشأنهم {إلا مراء ظاهرا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r5.claim: Do not ask the People of the Book about them after God has informed you.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162/r5.anchor: {ولا تستفت فيهم منهم} من أهل الكتاب {أحدا} أي: لا ترجع إلى قولهم بعد أن أخبرناك

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r1.claim: The predicted speakers are people discussing the youths’ story in the Prophet’s time, among the People of the Book and believers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r1.anchor: أي الخائضون في قصتهم في عهد الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من أهل الكتاب

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r2.speaker: اليهود
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r2.claim: The three-and-dog claim is attributed either to Jews or to the Jacobite leader among Christians of Najran.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r2.anchor: قيل هو قول اليهود وقيل هو قول السيد من نصارى نجران

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r3.speaker: النصارى
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r3.claim: The five-and-dog claim is attributed either to Christians or their Nestorian al-ʿAqib.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r3.anchor: قاله النصارى أو العاقب منهم وكان نسطوريا

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r4.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb means offering an unseen report without access to it, or conjecturing, as in the expression for guessing by supposition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r4.anchor: يرمون رميا بالخبر الخفي الذي لا مطلع لهم عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r5.claim: The first two reports omit the future marker because it need not be repeated after conjunction with the construction already containing it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r5.anchor: وإنما لم يذكر بالسين اكتفاء بعطفه على ما هو فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r6.claim: The seven-and-dog view is correct: Muslims learned it from the Prophet via Gabriel, and the wording signals it; the earlier two views are called guesses, while the conjunction marks the dog’s firmly attached description.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r6.anchor: إنما قاله المسلمون بإخبار الرسول لهم عن جبريل عليهما الصلاة والسلام وإيماء الله تعالى إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r7.speaker: علي
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r7.claim: Ali reports seven youths—Yamlikha, Makshaliniya, Mashliniya, Marnush, Dabarnush, Shadhnush, and a shepherd—with their dog Qitmir in Ephesus.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r7.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه هم سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم وأسماؤهم: يمليخا

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r8.claim: Another view attributes all three competing counts to the People of the Book, with only a few knowing the matter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r8.anchor: وقيل الأقوال الثلاثة لأهل الكتاب والقليل منهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r9.claim: Debate only openly from the Qur’anic account without insulting or deeply disputing; do not seek their guidance because revelation suffices and they lack knowledge, or question them merely to expose them against good manners.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:22/r9.anchor: فلا تجادل في شأن الفتية إلا جدالا ظاهرا غير متعمق فيه

DURR-FULL:v5p376/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r1.claim: The few who knew the youths' number were right: they were seven.
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r1.anchor: قوله: {ما يعلمهم إلا قليل} قال: إنا من القليل كانوا سبعة

DURR-FULL:v5p376/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r2.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas counts himself among the few and names the youths, including Tamlīkha, sent with the coin, and their shepherd; their dog was Qitmir.
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ما يعلمهم إلا قليل} قال: أنا من القليل مكسلمينا وتمليخا وهو المبعوث بالورق

DURR-FULL:v5p376/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r3.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman says he heard that writing the youths' names and throwing them into a fire calms it.
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن: بلغني أن من كتب هذه الأسماء في شيء وطرحه في حريق سكن الحريق

DURR-FULL:v5p376/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r4.claim: Wahb says Quranic references to a few mean fewer than ten.
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r4.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه قال: كل شي في القرآن قليل وإلا قليل فهو دون العشرة

DURR-FULL:v5p376/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r5.claim: The account God related is sufficient; there is no need to dispute further.
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {فلا تمار فيهم} يقول: حسبك ما قصصت عليك

DURR-FULL:v5p376/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r6.claim: Debate only what God disclosed, and do not ask the Jews beyond that account.
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا} قال: يقول: إلا ما أظهرنا لك من أمرهم

DURR-FULL:v5p376/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r7.claim: What God has related about the youths is sufficient.
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r7.anchor:
عن قتادة في قوله: {فلا تمار فيهم} الآية
قال: حسبك ما قصصنا عليك

DURR-FULL:v5p376/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r8.claim: The people from whom the Prophet should not seek an answer are the Jews.
DURR-FULL:v5p376/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا} قال: اليهود

QUSHAYRI:v2p213/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p213/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p213/r1.claim: The rival counts of the youths contrast with the certainty that God is the fourth of three and sixth of five in His knowledge and presence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p213/r1.anchor: ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p213/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p213/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p213/r3.claim: The dog is fortunate that God repeatedly mentions it alongside the youths and counts it among them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p213/r3.anchor: كما كرر ذكرهم ، كرر ذكر كلبهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r10.claim: Human knowledge falls short of the youths' hidden states and number; what is concealed in their secrets and hearts is known to God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r10.anchor: أخبر أن علوم الناس متقاصرة عن عددهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r11.claim: The youths' number is in principle certain, yet people cannot know it by observation; only a few have knowledge of it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r11.anchor: وعددهم يعلم بالضرورة ، وهم لا يدركون بالمشاهدة

QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r12.claim: The dog is fortunate that the verse includes it when the youths are counted.
QUSHAYRI:v2p214/r12.anchor: ولما ذكرهم عد الكلب في جملتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r1.claim: Public speculation about the youths' number and sleep's duration continued after revelation; the Quran leaves the matter vague to train believers to avoid inquiries with no religious or human benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r1.anchor: فكانت مثار تخرصات في معرفة عددهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r2.claim: The unintroduced they means people or Muslims; discussing the count is not itself sinful, but no claim has proof, and the future tense predicts continued debate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r2.anchor: وضمير ( يقولون ) عائد إلى غير مذكور لأنه معلوم من المقام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r3.claim: Mentioning seven and eight does not hint that eight was the true number; the Quran explicitly calls unsupported guesses speculation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r3.anchor: وليس في الانتهاء إلى عدد الثمانية إيماء إلى أنه العدة في نفس الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r4.claim: A few people know the count because God informed them; Muhammad must be among them, and Ibn Abbas reportedly said he was one of the few.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r4.anchor: وقد أعلم الله أن قليلا من الخلق يعلمون عدتهم وهم من أطلعهم الله على ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly identified himself as one of the few who know their number.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r5.anchor: وروي أن ابن عباس قال : أنا من القليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r6.claim: People may have favored an odd number as auspicious, but there is no evidence for this, and God calls their assertion a guess at the unseen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r6.anchor: وكأن أقوال الناس تمالأت على أن عدتهم فردية تيمنا بعدد المفرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r7.claim: Rajm literally means throwing stones and is metaphorically used for speaking without reflection or verification; Zuhayr's poetry witnesses the figurative sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r7.anchor: والرجم حقيقته : الرمي بحجر ونحوه . واستعير هنا لرمي الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r8.claim: The first two clauses about the dog may each be an adjective of the preceding number or a second predicate of an omitted subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r8.anchor: وكل من جملة { رابعهم كلبهم } وجملة { سادسهم كلبهم } في موضع الصفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r9.claim: The waw before the eighth count marks a circumstantial clause, not an emphatic adjective; al-Sakkaki and other scholars reject al-Kashshaf's analysis as unidiomatic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p290#3/r9.anchor: ولا وجه لجعل الواو فيه داخلة على جملة هي صفة للنكرة لقصد تأكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r1.claim: The command to say that God knows best answers the audience's desire for a reliable count: God's knowledge is complete, while others' knowledge is conjectural.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r1.anchor: فأجيب بأن يحال العلم بذلك على علام الغيوب . وإسناد اسم التفضيل إلى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r2.claim: The statement that only a few know answers whether any human has partial knowledge; they must have been informed by God and remain less knowing than Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r2.anchor: فأجيب بأن قليلا من الناس يعلمون ذلك ولا محالة هم من أطلعهم الله على ذلك بوحي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r3.claim: If Meccan opponents dispute the number based on scriptural reports, the Prophet should not debate them because the issue has no useful consequence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r3.anchor: فلا تمارهم إذ هو اشتغال بما ليس فيه جدوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r4.claim: Mirāʾ derives from doubt and, through reciprocal verbal form, describes disputation that draws both sides into doubt; it became conventional for argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r4.anchor: والتماري : تفاعل مشتق من المرية ، وهي الشك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r5.claim: The permitted outward argument is brief and undeniable, such as saying God knows their number and only a few know it; further inquiry lacks evidence and benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p293/r5.anchor: والمراء الظاهر : هو الذي لا سبيل إلى إنكاره ولا يطول الخوض فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r1.claim: Istifta means seeking authoritative information about something not commonly known, and fi-him means concerning the sleepers' affair.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r1.anchor: والاستفتاء : طلب الفتوى ، وهي الخبر عن أمر علمي مما لا يعلمه كل أحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r2.claim: One reading takes the prohibition as implying that the Meccans who asked did not themselves know the story's details.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r2.anchor: والمراد من النهي عن استفتائهم الكناية عن جهلهم بأمر أهل الكهف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r3.claim: Alternatively, the prohibition can imply that the Prophet already knows the truth from God and need not ask, while he is not commanded to satisfy the challengers; Ibn Ashur says this explains the prohibition's purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r3.anchor: أو يكون كناية رمزية عن حصول علم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بحقيقة أمرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r4.claim: The phrase from among them cannot refer to the People of the Book, since transmitters and commentators agree that the surah is Meccan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p294/r4.anchor: لأن هذه الآيات مكية باتفاق الرواة والمفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses thalāthatun as the predicate of an implied subject: those disputing say the youths were three.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r1.anchor: ثلاثة مرفوع بخبر الابتداء المعنى سيقول الذين تنازعوا في أمرهم هم ثلاثة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r2.claim: One view says the speakers were Christians of Najran debating the Prophet; Melkites said three, Jacobites five, and Nestorians seven, each counting the dog.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r2.anchor: أنهم نصارى نجران ناظروا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في عدة أهل الكهف فقالت الملكية هم ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r3.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi says the speakers were the people of the youths’ city before they were discovered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r3.anchor: أنهم أهل مدينتهم قبل ظهورهم عليهم ذكره الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r4.speaker: زهير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r4.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb means conjecturing without certainty; Zuhayr’s line uses marjum to mean unsupported report.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r4.anchor: وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتم وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives one grammatical view that the presence or absence of the conjunction wāw is equivalent.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r6.speaker: أبو نصر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r6.claim: Abu Nasr says the wāw before eighth makes clear that a wāw was intended in the preceding clauses but omitted for lightness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r6.anchor: أن ظهور الواو في الجملة الثامنة دلالة على على أنها مرادة في الجملتين المتقدمتين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج ومقاتل بن سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Muqatil say the wāw marks the end of the reported disagreement; al-Thaʿlabi calls it a wāw of judgment, affirming the Muslims’ count of seven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r7.anchor: أن دخولها يدل على انقطاع القصة وان الكلام قد تم ذكره الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r8.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi says Arabs may mark eight after seven because seven completes a counting set, pointing to descriptions in 9:112 and 39:71–73.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p124#2/r8.anchor: أن العرب تعطف بالواو على السبعة فيقولون ستة سبعة وثمانية لأن العقد عندهم سبعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the youths numbered seven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r1.anchor: احدهما أنهم كانوا سبعة قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r2.speaker: ابن جريج وابن اسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Ishaq say the youths numbered eight; Ibn al-Anbari says the eighth was the dog’s owner, as in saying generosity means Hatim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r2.anchor: والثاني ثمانية قاله ابن جريج وابن اسحاق وقال ابن الأنباري وقيل معنى قوله وثامنهم كلبهم صاحب كلبهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r3.speaker: هشيم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r3.claim: Hushaym lists the youths’ names as Mكسلمينا, Yamlikha, Tarinus, Sadinus, Sarinus, Nawasis, and Yaranus; the tafsir records disagreement and omits details.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r3.anchor: وأما أسماؤهم فقال هشيم مكسلمينا ويمليخا وطرينوس وسدينوس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the dog belonged to a shepherd they passed, and both shepherd and dog followed them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r4.anchor: أنه كان لراع مروا به فتبعهم الراعي والكلب قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r5.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r5.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr says the dog belonged to them and they used it for hunting.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r5.anchor: انه كان لهم يتصيدون عليه قاله عبيد بن عمير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r6.speaker: كعب الأحبار
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r6.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar says a stray dog repeatedly returned after they drove it away, declared love for God’s beloved, and slept guarding them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r6.anchor: ما تريدون مني لا تخشوا جانبي انا أحب أحباء الله فناموا حتى أحرسكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r7.claim: Abu Salih reports from Ibn Abbas that the dog’s name was Qitmir.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r7.anchor: قطمير قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r8.claim: Another report names the dog Raqim, attributed to Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r8.anchor: اسمه الرقيم وقد ذكرناه عن سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r9.claim: Abd Allah ibn Kathir gives the dog’s name as Qatmur.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r9.anchor: قطمور قاله عبد الله بن كثير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r10.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r10.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʾi gives the dog’s name as Hamran.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r11.speaker: الثوري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r11.claim: Al-Thawri says the dog was red.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r12.speaker: ابن اسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r12.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the dog was yellow.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r13.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r13.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib describes the dog as red-headed, black-backed, white-bellied, with a spotted tail.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r13.anchor: أحمر الرأس أسود الظهر أبيض البطن أبلق الذنب ذكره ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r14.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r14.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, and Abu Amr vocalize the yāʾ in rabbī; the remaining readers leave it unvocalized.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r14.anchor: حرك الياء ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وأسكنها الباقون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r15.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r15.claim: Ata says the few who know the youths’ number are People of the Book; Ibn Abbas says he is among them and counts seven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r15.anchor: قال عطاء يعني بالقليل أهل الكتاب قال ابن عباس أنا من ذلك القليل هم سعبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r16.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada say not to dispute about the youths because the revealed account is sufficient.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r16.anchor: لا تمار أحدا حسبك ما قصصت عليك من أمرهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r17.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r17.claim: Ibn Zayd says debate their number only to the extent of telling opponents their claim is wrong.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r17.anchor: لا تمار في عدتهم إلا مراء ظاهرا أن تقول لهم ليس كما تقولون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r18.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r18.claim: A further view says the permitted exchange is an argument supported by clear proof.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r18.anchor: إلا مراء ظاهرا بحجة واضحة حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r19.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r19.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r19.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says not to argue beyond a certain, informed account from God, unmixed with falsehood; the word mirāʾ is linked to drawing out an opponent’s anger, like milking a sheep.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p125/r19.anchor: لا تجادل إلا جدال متيقن عالم بحقيقة الخبر إذ الله تعالى ألقى إليك مالا يشوبه باطل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127/r1.claim: The prohibition on seeking a ruling about the youths means not to ask the People of the Book, according to Ibn Abbas.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127/r1.anchor: في أصحاب الكهف منهم قال ابن عباس يعني من أهل الكتاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127/r2.claim: Al-Farra says Nestorian and Jacobite Christian groups came to the Prophet, who asked them the youths’ number and was then prohibited from asking.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127/r2.anchor: أتاه فريقان من النصارى نسطوري ويعقوبي فسألهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عددهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects the first two proposed counts as guesses and infers that the third, seven youths plus their dog, is correct from the verse’s wording.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r1.anchor: ولما ضعف القولين الأولين بقوله: {رجما بالغيب} أي: قولا بلا علم، كمن (9) يرمي إلى مكان لا يعرفه، فإنه لا يكاد يصيب، وإن أصاب فبلا قصد، ثم حكى الثالث وسكت عليه أو قرره بقوله: {وثامنهم كلبهم} فدل على صحته،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r2.claim: Where there is no need to know a detail and no reliable revelation about it, the sound course is to leave its knowledge to God and stop at the revealed account.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r2.anchor: وقوله: {قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم} إرشاد إلى أن الأحسن في مثل هذا المقام رد العلم إلى الله تعالى، إذ لا احتياج إلى الخوض في مثل ذلك بلا علم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says he is among the few who know the youths numbered seven; Qatada and Ibn Jurayj through Ata al-Khurasani report the same view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: {ما يعلمهم إلا قليل} أي: من الناس. قال قتادة: قال ابن عباس: أنا من القليل الذي استثنى الله، عز وجل، كانوا سبعة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits Ibn Abbas saying he is among the few and that the youths numbered seven; Ibn Kathir calls the chains to Ibn Abbas sound and the count consistent with the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r4.anchor: حدثنا إسرائيل، عن سماك، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: {ما يعلمهم إلا قليل} قال: أنا من القليل، كانوا سبعة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports from Mujahid a detailed account naming eight youths; Ibn Kathir cautions that the names may come from Ibn Ishaq or an intermediary because the reliable Ibn Abbas report says seven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار عن عبد الله بن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد قال: لقد حدثت أنه كان على بعضهم من حداثة سنه وضح الورق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r6.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r6.claim: Shuayb al-Jubai names the dog Himran, but Ibn Kathir doubts the reliability of these personal and dog names because most were received from the People of the Book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r6.anchor: وقد تقدم عن شعيب الجبائي أن اسم كلبهم حمران (7) ، وفي تسميتهم بهذه (8) الأسماء واسم كلبهم نظر في صحته، والله أعلم؛ فإن غالب ذلك متلقى من أهل الكتاب،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r7.claim: The command to argue only briefly means a simple, easy exchange because knowing the exact count yields little benefit; the Prophet should not ask the People of the Book, who speculate without authoritative evidence, since God’s truth judges earlier books and claims.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147#2/r7.anchor: وقد قال تعالى: {فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا} أي: سهلا هينا؛ فإن الأمر في معرفة (9) ذلك لا يترتب عليه كبير (10) فائدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r1.claim: Those who debated the Sleepers' number around Muhammad asked him, and revelation foretold their future disagreement; the accurate view is seven and their dog eighth, with Ibn Abbas counting himself among the few who know.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r1.anchor: الضمير لمن خاض في قصتهم في زمن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أهل الكتاب والمؤمنين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says he is one of the few who know the Sleepers' number.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : أنا من أولئك القليل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r3.speaker: السيد والعاقب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r3.claim: In a report about Christians from Najran with the Prophet, the Jacobite leader says three and the Nestorian leader says five, while the Muslims say seven; God confirms the Muslims' number, learned from Gabriel's revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r3.anchor: فقال السيد وكان يعقوبيا : كانوا ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r4.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r4.claim: Ali names the seven sleepers, their positions among King Decianus's advisers, the shepherd who joined them, their city Ephesus, and their dog's name Qitmir.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r4.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه : هم سبعة نفر أسماؤهم : يمليخا ، ومكشليتيا ، ومشلينيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r5.claim: The future sīn may scope over both later statements, or the imperfect verbs may themselves carry future meaning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r5.anchor: فإن قلت : لم جاء بسين الاستقبال في الأول دون الآخرين ؟ قلت : فيه وجهان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r6.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb means throwing out hidden information, like the Qur'anic use of throwing something in the unseen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r6.anchor: رجما بالغيب } رميا بالخبر الخفي وإتيانا به كقوله { ويقذفون بالغيب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#2/r7.claim: Rajm may be idiomatic for supposition because Arabs used rajm al-ẓann so often for guessing; Zuhayr's line uses it for a conjectured account.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r1.claim: The word in Zuhayr's citation means conjectured; another reading merges the thāʾ of thalāth with the feminine tāʾ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r1.anchor: أي المظنون . وقرىء ( ثلاث رابعهم ) بإدغام الثاء في تاء التأنيث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r2.claim: Three, five, and seven predicate omitted they; each following phrase about their dog is a clause describing that number.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r2.anchor: ثلاثة } خبر مبتدأ محذوف ، أي : هم ثلاثة . وكذلك { خمسة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r3.claim: The conjunction waw appears before the third description because a descriptive clause may take waw, which reinforces its attachment and the stable, confident quality of the claim.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r3.anchor: هي الواو التي تدخل على الجملة الواقعة صفة للنكرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says that once the waw appears, the count stops; no further number needs consideration.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : حين وقعت الواو انقطعت العدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r5.claim: Another view takes the few who know to be a small number of the People of the Book; most of them only guess.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r5.anchor: وقيل : إلا قليل من أهل الكتاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r6.claim: Do not argue about the Sleepers beyond what revelation states; present it plainly without humiliating or scolding the People of the Book, following the command to debate graciously.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r6.anchor: فلا تجادل أهل الكتاب في شأن أصحاب الكهف إلا جدالا ظاهرا غير متعمق فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r7.claim: Do not question them either to trap them or to seek instruction, because God has already revealed the story.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p666#3/r7.anchor: ولا تسأل أحدا منهم عن قصتهم سؤال متعنت له ، حتى يقول شيئا فترده عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r1.claim: The conjunction wāw marks the break between a completed report and what follows.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r1.anchor: فأدخل الواو على انقطاع القصة لأن الخبر قد تم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r2.claim: The disputants about the sleepers’ number may have been people of Medina before the matter was disclosed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم أهل المدينة قبل الظهور عليهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r3.claim: Alternatively, they were People of the Book after a long passage of time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r3.anchor: الثاني : أنهم أهل الكتاب بعد طول العهد بهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r4.claim: Rajman bi-l-ghayb means conjecturing or throwing out a guess.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { رجما بالغيب } قال قتادة قذفا بالظن ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r5.speaker: زهير
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r5.claim: Zuhayr’s verse says war is known by experience rather than conjectural talk, illustrating the word for a conjectured report.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r5.anchor: وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتم … وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says he is among the few exceptioned by God: there were seven sleepers and their dog was the eighth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : أنا من القليل الذي استثنى الله تعالى : كانوا سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r7.speaker: ابن جريج ومحمد بن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Ishaq say there were eight, construing the phrase about the eighth as “companion of their dog.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جريج ومحمد بن إسحاق : كانوا ثمانية , وجعلا قوله تعالى : { وثامنهم كلبهم } أي صاحب كلبهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r8.claim: Their people wrote down the sleepers’ names when they disappeared; after their case became known, names were inscribed on the cave door.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r8.anchor: وكتب قومهم أسماءهم حين غابوا , فلما بان أمرهم كتبت أسماؤهم على باب الكهف .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj lists their names; Yamlikha carried money to buy food.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r9.anchor: قال ابن جريج : أسماؤهم مكسلمينا ويمليخا وهو الذي مضى بالورق يشتري به الطعام , ومطرونس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r10.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r10.claim: Muqatil says the dog belonged to Maksalmina, the oldest sleeper, who owned sheep.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r10.anchor: قال مقاتل : وكان الكلب لمكسلمينا وكان أسنهم وكان صاحب غنم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r11.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r11.claim: Do not dispute beyond what God has already disclosed about the sleepers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r11.anchor: أحدها : إلا ما قد أظهرنا لك من أمرهم , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r12.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r12.claim: What has already been related is enough; do not ask for further disclosure.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r12.anchor: الثاني : حسبك ما قصصا عليك من شأنهم , فلا تسألني عن إظهار غيره , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r13.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r13.claim: The permitted discussion is argument supported by clear proof and truthful report.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r13.anchor: الثالث : إلا مراء ظاهرا يعني بحجة واضحة وخبر صادق , قاله علي بن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r14.claim: Do not debate anyone about them except by telling an account.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r14.anchor: الرابع : لا تجادل فيهم أحدا ألا أن تحدثهم به حديثا , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r15.claim: The instruction may mean testifying before people concerning the sleepers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r15.anchor: الخامس : هو أن تشهد الناس عليهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r16.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r16.claim: Do not ask any of the People of the Book about the sleepers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r16.anchor: أحدهما : ولا تستفت يا محمد فيهم أحدا من أهل الكتاب , قاله ابن عباس . ومجاهد وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r17.claim: Alternatively, the address is to the Prophet while the prohibition applies to his community.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p296/r17.anchor: الثاني : أنه خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ونهي لأمته .

MUJAHID:v1p375#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p375#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p375#2/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the people whom the Prophet should not consult about the Cave Companions as the Jews.
MUJAHID:v1p375#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ولا تستفت فيهم ﴾ يعني اليهود

MUQATIL:18:22/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:22/r1.speaker: نصارى نجران
MUQATIL:18:22/r1.claim: Christians of Najran proposed three youths and a fourth dog or five and a sixth dog; the verse calls these guesses without knowledge.
MUQATIL:18:22/r1.anchor: { سيقولون } ، يعني نصارى نجران: الفتية { ثلاثة } نفر، { رابعهم كلبهم ويقولون خمسة سادسهم كلبهم }

MUQATIL:18:22/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:22/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:22/r2.claim: He gives seven youths and the dog as the account; only a few, including Nestorians, know their number.
MUQATIL:18:22/r2.anchor: { ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم } ، وإنما صاروا بالواو واو؛ لأنه انقطع الكلام،

MUQATIL:18:22/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:22/r3.speaker: أبو العباس ثعلب
MUQATIL:18:22/r3.claim: Tha'lab says the waw before 'eighth' is a circumstantial waw describing their state when the dog is mentioned.
MUQATIL:18:22/r3.anchor: وقال أبو العباس ثعلب: ألفوا هذه الواو الحال، كان المعنى: هذه حالهم عند ذكر الكلب،

MUQATIL:18:22/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:22/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:22/r4.claim: The first counts were held by Najran's leaders al-Sayyid and al-Aqib and Jacobite followers; debate only from the Qur'an's true account and ask no Christian about it.
MUQATIL:18:22/r4.anchor: هذا قول نصارى نجران السيد والعاقب ومن معهما من المار يعقوبيين، وهم حزب النصارى،

NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r1.claim: Those discussing the story in the Prophet’s time—believers and People of the Book who asked him—would differ after he delayed his answer pending revelation; the correct count is seven with their dog eighth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r1.anchor: الضمير في سيقولون لمن خاض في قصتهم في زمن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من المؤمنين واهل الكتاب سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عنهم فأخر الجواب إلى أن يوحى إليه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r2.speaker: السيد
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r2.claim: The Jacobite leader al-Sayyid said the youths were three, with their dog fourth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r2.anchor: فقال السيد وكان يعقوبيا كانوا ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r3.speaker: العاقب
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r3.claim: The Nestorian al-ʿAqib said they were five, with their dog sixth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r3.anchor: وقال العاقب وكان نسطوريا كانوا خمسة سادسهم كلبهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r4.speaker: المسلمون
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r4.claim: The Muslims said seven with the dog eighth; God confirmed their view, which they knew through the Messenger’s report and the prior account.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r4.anchor: وقال المسلمون كانوا سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم فحفق الله قول المسلمين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r5.speaker: علي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r5.claim: Ali names seven: six counselors to King Decius, three at his right and three at his left, plus a shepherd who joined their flight; the city was Ephesus and the dog Qitmir.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r5.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه هم سبعة نفر أسماؤهم بمليخا ومكشلينا ومشليينا هؤلاء أصحاب يمين الملك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r6.claim: Although future sin appears only in the first report, it governs the later reports too; alternatively, the present verb carries future meaning.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r6.anchor: وسين الاستقبال وان دخل في الاول دون الآخرين فهما داخلان في حكم السين كقولك قد أكرم وأنعم تريد معنى التوقع في الفعلين جميعا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r7.claim: Three, five, and seven are predicates of omitted ‘they are’; ‘their dog fourth/sixth/eighth’ is a clause adjectivally describing each number.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p9/r7.anchor: ثلاثة خبر متبدأ محذوف أي هم ثلاثة وكذلك خمسة وسبعة ورابعهم كلبهم جملة من مبتدأ وخبر واقعة صفة لثلاثة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r1.claim: رجم بالغيب means conjecturing hidden information, likened to throwing at the unseen or to casting an unknown report.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r1.anchor: بالغيب رميا بالخبر الخفي واتيانا به كقوله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r2.claim: Alternatively, throwing stones is used for supposition because people came to use the two expressions without distinction.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r2.anchor: أووضع الرجم موضع الظن مكانه قيل ظنا بالغيب لأنهم أكثروا أن يقولوا رجم بالظن مكان قولهم ظن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r3.claim: The waw before the third statement marks a clause qualifying an indefinite noun and emphasizes a settled attribute.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r3.anchor: والواو الداخلة على الجملة الثالثة هي الواو التي تدخل على الجملة الواقعة صفة للنكرة كما تدخل على الواقعة حالا عن المعرفة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r4.claim: The waw signals that those who say seven with the dog eighth speak from firm knowledge rather than conjecture.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r4.anchor: وهذه الواو التي آذنت بأن الذين قالوا سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم قالوه عن ثبات علم ولم يرجموا بالظن كما رجم غيرهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r5.claim: God’s statement that He knows their number confirms the seven-count; Ibn ʿAbbas says he is one of the few who know it, while another view identifies the few as learned People of the Book.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r5.anchor: أي قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم وقد أخبركم بها بقوله سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم ﴿ ما يعلمهم إلا قليل ﴾ قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنا من ذلك القليل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r6.claim: Alternatively, the few who know are from the People of the Book; most of them rely on guesswork.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r6.anchor: وقيل إلا قليل من أهل الكتاب والضمير في سيقولون على هذا الأهل الكتاب خاصة أي سيقولون أهل الكتاب فيهم كذا وكذا ولا علم بذلك إلا في قليل منهم وأكثرهم على ظن وتخمين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r7.claim: Do not argue deeply with the People of the Book; simply repeat what God revealed, without humiliating them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r7.anchor: فلا تجادل أهل الكتاب في شأن اصحاب الكهف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r8.claim: Another explanation is to debate in public so the Prophet’s truth is evident.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r8.anchor: أو بمشهد من الناس ليظهر صدقك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r9.claim: Do not ask them about the story, whether to entrap and refute them or seek guidance, since God has already disclosed it to the Prophet.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10/r9.anchor: ولا تسأل أحدا منهم عن قصتهم سؤال متعنت له حتى يقول شيئا فترده عليه وتزيف ما عنده ولا سؤال مسترشد لأن الله تعالى قد ارشد بأن أوحى إليك قصتهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266/r1.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb is conjecture without certainty.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#3/r6.claim: The three- and five-youth counts are speculation, while the seven-count is followed by a command to say God knows best and not to dispute or consult the Jews.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#3/r6.anchor: ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم ما يعلمهم إلا قليل

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#3/r7.claim: The command not to debate means avoid disputing them beyond an outward discussion, and do not consult people who lack knowledge of the youths.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#3/r7.anchor: أي لا تكابرهم { إلا مرآء ظاهرا ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا } فإنهم لا علم لهم بهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r1.claim: The pronoun in سيقولون may refer to the People of the Torah and Muhammad's contemporaries, who disputed the sleepers' number.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r1.anchor: الضمير في «سيقولون» يراد به أهل التوراة ومعاصري محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r2.claim: Another account says Christians from Najran came to the Prophet: Jacobites said three, Nestorians five, and Muslims seven.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r2.anchor: فقالت اليعقوبية: كانوا ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم. وقالت النسطورية: كانوا خمسة سادسهم كلبهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r3.claim: A further view says the verse reports Jews who instructed polytheists to question the Prophet about the Companions.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو إخبار عن اليهود الذين أمروا المشركين بمسألة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أصحاب الكهف.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r4.speaker: النحويون
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r4.claim: Grammarians treat the waw in وثامنهم as conjunction in the final report, setting it apart and signaling the last proposed number; the sentence works without it.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r4.anchor: طريق النحويين أنها واو عطف دخلت في آخر إخبار عن عددهم لتفصل أمرهم،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r5.speaker: ابن خالويه
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r5.claim: Ibn Khalawayh and a group call it the waw of eight.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r5.anchor: وقالت فرقة منها ابن خالويه: هي واو الثمانية.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r6.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash says Quraysh inserted waw when counting six, seven, and eight.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r6.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي عن أبي بكر بن عياش أن قريشا كانت تقول في عددها ستة سبعة وثمانية

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r7.speaker: القفال
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r7.claim: Al-Qaffal says Arab counting ended at seven and restarted with waw; he cites 9:112, the gates in 39:71–73, and أبكارا in 66:5.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r7.anchor: وحكى نحوه القفال، فقال: إن قوما قالوا العدد ينتهي عند العرب إلى سبعة،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r8.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r8.claim: Al-Qushayri calls the seven-ending theory arbitrary and refutes it with God's names in 59:23, where no waw introduces an eighth name.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r8.anchor: قال القشيري أبو نصر: ومثل هذا الكلام تحكم، ومن أين السبعة نهاية عندهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r9.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r9.claim: Those favoring seven say waw marks this count as true and distinct: earlier estimates are conjecture while this one is not criticized.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r9.anchor: وقال قوم ممن صار إلى أن عددهم سبعة: إنما ذكر الواو في قوله: «سبعة وثامنهم»

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r10.claim: رجم means conjectural speech; the source illustrates the word with a poem about war and an unfounded report.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22/r10.anchor: والرجم: القول بالظن يقال لكل ما يخرص: رجم فيه ومرجوم ومرجم كما قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r1.claim: A quoted line uses مرجم for a conjectural report.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r1.anchor: وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتم وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج ومحمد بن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r2.claim: They say there were eight and take وثامنهم كلبهم to mean the dog's eighth companion; Qurtubi says this supports the grammarians' conjunction analysis.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جريج ومحمد بن إسحاق كانوا ثمانية، وجعلا قوله تعالى: «وثامنهم كلبهم» أي صاحب كلبهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r3.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r3.claim: Al-Qushayri says waw could have appeared with fourth or sixth instead; seeking its placement's hidden cause is strained, as with 15:4 and 26:208–209.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r3.anchor: وقال القشيري: لم يذكر الواو في قوله: رابعهم سادسهم، ولو كان بالعكس لكان جائزا،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r4.claim: God instructs the Prophet to return the number to Him; only a few humans know it, which Ata takes to mean some People of the Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r4.anchor: أمر الله تعالى نبيه عليه السلام في هذه الآية أن يرد علم عدتهم إليه عز وجل.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says he is among the few: the youths were seven and their brindled dog Qitmir was between two breeds in size.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r5.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول: أنا من ذلك القليل، كانوا سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم، ثم ذكر السبعة بأسمائهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Said ibn al-Musayyib says the dog was Chinese; Qurtubi prefers the report that it was Zubayri.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r6.anchor: وقال محمد بن سعيد بن المسيب: هو كلب صيني. والصحيح أنه زبيري.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r7.speaker: محمد بن سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r7.claim: He says nearly every hadith scholar in Nishapur wrote this report from him; Abu Amr al-Hiri wrote it too.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r7.anchor: وقال: ما بقي بنيسابور محدث إلا كتب عني هذا الحديث إلا من لم يقدر له.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r8.claim: The Prophet should dispute only outwardly, using revelation or saying the others are wrong, without arguing over a fixed count.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r8.anchor: أي لا تجادل في أصحاب الكهف إلا بما أوحيناه إليك وهو رد علم عدتهم إلى الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r9.claim: The wording does not truly license disputation; it figuratively describes answering People of the Book in a manifest way.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r9.anchor: ولم يبح له في هذه الآية أن يماري ولكن قوله: «إلا مراء» استعارة

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r10.claim: فيهم refers to the Cave Companions, منهم to opposing People of the Book, and the omitted object of dispute is their number.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r10.anchor: والضمير في قوله: «فيهم» عائد على أهل الكهف. وفي قوله «منهم» عائد على أهل الكتاب المعارضين.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r11.claim: A report says the Prophet asked Christians of Najran about the Companions and was forbidden; Qurtubi sees proof against Muslims consulting People of the Book on knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:22#2/r11.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام سأل نصارى نجران عنهم فنهي عن السؤال.

STUDYQURAN:18:22/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r1.claim: The verse discourages debate over the youths’ number because it is speculation about the unseen, which belongs to God.
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r1.anchor: all such debate amounts to guessing at the unseen, a vain endeavor

STUDYQURAN:18:22/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r2.claim: Some identify the few who know the youths’ number as the People of the Book.
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r2.anchor: Some identify the “few” here as the People of the Book (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:18:22/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r3.claim: The command to dispute only with clear argument addresses the Prophet, who should let the Quranic account suffice instead of debating them.
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r3.anchor: instructs him not to debate with them about the matter, but rather to let the parts of the story that had been revealed to him in this Quranic account suffice

STUDYQURAN:18:22/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r4.claim: The Prophet is also told not to question the People of the Book further about the story.
STUDYQURAN:18:22/r4.anchor: meaning that he should not question the People of the Book further about this matter (Ṭ).

TAB-FULL:v15p217/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p217/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p217/r1.claim: The claims that the youths numbered three or five are conjecture without certain knowledge; rajman bi-l-ghayb means casting an uncertain guess.
TAB-FULL:v15p217/r1.anchor: رجما بالغيب} [الكهف: 22] يقول: قذفا بالظن غير يقين علم

TAB-FULL:v15p217/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p217/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p217/r2.claim: Qatada glosses rajman bi-l-ghayb as a guess cast into the unseen.
TAB-FULL:v15p217/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم ويقولون خمسة سادسهم كلبهم رجما بالغيب} [الكهف: 22] أي قذفا بالغيب

TAB-FULL:v15p217/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p217/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p217/r3.claim: An anonymous poet’s line uses marjum for something made the subject of a guess.
TAB-FULL:v15p217/r3.anchor: كما قال الشاعر: [البحر الطويل] وأجعل مني الحق غيبا مرجما

TAB-FULL:v15p219/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r1.claim: God says that only a few of His creatures know the youths’ number.
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r1.anchor: يقول: ما يعلم عددهم {إلا قليل} [النساء: 66] من خلقه

TAB-FULL:v15p219/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r2.claim: Qatada interprets the few who know as a small number of people.
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {ما يعلمهم إلا قليل} [الكهف: 22] يقول: قليل من الناس

TAB-FULL:v15p219/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r3.claim: Another view takes the few who know as the People of the Book.
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عنى بالقليل: أهل الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v15p219/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says he is among the exception, and that the youths were seven.
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r4.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول: أنا ممن استثناه الله، ويقول: عدتهم سبعة

TAB-FULL:v15p219/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r5.claim: A further Ibn Abbas report also says the youths numbered seven and he was among the few.
TAB-FULL:v15p219/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ما يعلمهم إلا قليل} [الكهف: 22] قال: أنا من القليل، كانوا سبعة

TAB-FULL:v15p220/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p220/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p220/r1.claim: The Prophet is told not to argue with the People of the Book about the youths’ number; “number” is omitted because listeners know the intended subject.
TAB-FULL:v15p220/r1.anchor: حدثني يونس، قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب، قال: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {فلا تمار فيهم} [الكهف: 22] قال: لا تمار في عدتهم

TAB-FULL:v15p220/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p220/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p220/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the instruction means not to dispute their number.
TAB-FULL:v15p220/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {فلا تمار فيهم} [الكهف: 22] قال: لا تمار في عدتهم

TAB-FULL:v15p221/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the allowed apparent discussion is limited to what God has already recounted.
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا} [الكهف: 22] يقول: حسبك ما قصصت عليك فلا تمار فيهم

TAB-FULL:v15p221/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r2.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet may discuss only what God has made known about them.
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، {فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا} [الكهف: 22] يقول: إلا بما قد أظهرنا لك من أمرهم

TAB-FULL:v15p221/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r3.claim: Qatada says the revealed account of their story is enough; the Prophet should not go beyond it.
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا} [الكهف: 22] أي حسبك ما قصصنا عليك من شأنهم

TAB-FULL:v15p221/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise says the Qur’anic account is sufficient.
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r4.anchor: يقول في قوله: {فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا} [الكهف: 22] يقول: حسبك ما قصصنا عليك

TAB-FULL:v15p221/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets apparent discussion as telling disputants their proposed numbers are wrong because they do not know the count.
TAB-FULL:v15p221/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {إلا مراء ظاهرا} [الكهف: 22] قال: أن يقول لهم: ليس كما تقولون، ليس تعلمون عدتهم

TAB-FULL:v15p223/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r1.claim: The Prophet must not ask any People of the Book about the youths’ number, since their guesses are not certain knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا} [الكهف: 22] قال: هم أهل الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v15p223/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the people from whom the Prophet should not seek an answer as the People of the Book.
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا} [الكهف: 22] قال: هم أهل الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v15p223/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies them as Jews and says not to ask Jews beyond what God has already told the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد {ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا} [الكهف: 22] من يهود، قال: ولا تسأل يهود عن أمر أصحاب الكهف

TAB-FULL:v15p223/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r4.claim: Qatada reports that the cave youths were Roman kings called Banū al-Raknā who accepted Islam, separated from their people, and withdrew to the cave; a Muslim people and king followed.
TAB-FULL:v15p223/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا} [الكهف: 22] من أهل الكتاب، كنا نحدث أنهم كانوا بني الركنا، والركنا: ملوك الروم، رزقهم الله الإسلام

THALABI:v6p162/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p162/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p162/r1.claim: At a meeting with the Prophet, Najran’s Christian leaders differed: Sayyid, a Jacobite, said three; al-Aqib, a Nestorian, said five; Muslims said seven. The Quran confirms the Muslim view.
THALABI:v6p162/r1.anchor: أن السيد والعاقب وأصحابهما من نصارى أهل نجران كانوا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v6p162/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p162/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p162/r2.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb means conjecture without certainty; the cited poem witnesses this sense of rajm.
THALABI:v6p162/r2.anchor: أي قذفا بالظن من غير يقين، كقول الشاعر: وأجعل مني الحق غيبا مرجما

THALABI:v6p162/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p162/r3.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v6p162/r3.claim: One view calls the conjunction before ‘eight’ the waw of eight: Arabs counted in groups of seven, as illustrated by three Quranic passages.
THALABI:v6p162/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذه الواو واو الثمانية، إن العرب يقولون: واحد، اثنان، ثلاثة،

THALABI:v6p162/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p162/r4.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v6p162/r4.claim: Another view calls it a waw of judgment and confirmation: the quotation ends at ‘seven,’ then the text confirms the dog was eighth, supporting the Muslim count.
THALABI:v6p162/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذه واو الحكم والتحقيق، فكأنه حكى اختلافهم فتم الكلام

THALABI:v6p162/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p162/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p162/r5.claim: He says only a few people know the sleepers’ number.

THALABI:v6p162/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p162/r6.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v6p162/r6.claim: He identifies the few who know the number as People of Scripture.
THALABI:v6p162/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء: يعني بالقليل: أهل الكتاب.

THALABI:v6p162/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p162/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p162/r7.claim: He says he himself is one of the few who know their number.
THALABI:v6p162/r7.anchor: عن أبيه عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى. ما يعلمهم إلا قليل قال:

THALABI:v6p162/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p162/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p162/r8.claim: The seven sleepers are listed by name; their brindled dog is Qitmir, a breed between a Qalti and a Kurdish dog. Muhammad ibn al-Musayyib calls the Qalti Chinese.

THALABI:v6p162/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p162/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p162/r9.claim: Do not dispute their number or ask People of Scripture; the Quran’s account is enough, and discussion should stay with what it plainly tells.
THALABI:v6p162/r9.anchor: فلا تمار فيهم، أي في عدتهم وشأنهم إلا مراء ظاهرا وهو ما قص عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r1.claim: Commentators recount that Christians from Najran discussed the Cave Companions with the Prophet: Jacobites said three, Nestorians five, and Muslims seven.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r2.claim: The verse's future tense places this dispute after revelation; the surah is Meccan, whereas the Najran delegation came after the Hijra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r2.anchor: ونظم الآية يوجب أن يكون هذا التنازع بعد نزول الآية؛ لأن الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r3.speaker: النحويون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r3.claim: Grammarians agree that 'three' is a predicate-less initial subject understood as 'they are three,' but differ over the absent conjunction before 'fourth' and 'sixth' and its presence before 'eighth.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r3.anchor: واختلف النحويون في نظم هذه الآية وسقوط الواو من قولهم: رابعهم وسادسهم، ودخولها في ثامنهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r4.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r4.claim: The Sahib al-Nazm takes 'their dog is fourth' as a subject-predicate clause in the circumstantial position of 'three,' meaning they say three with this circumstance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r5.speaker: أبو الفتح الموصلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r5.claim: Abu al-Fath rejects that circumstantial analysis: 'they are three' supplies nothing that can govern the circumstantial clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r5.anchor: قال أبو الفتح الموصلي: (لا يجوز أن تكون الجملة حالا لثلاثة؛ لأنك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r6.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r6.claim: Another grammatical view makes 'fourth' an adjective of 'three' and treats 'their dog' as raised by the participle, by analogy with a participle governing its subject.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: ({رابعهم} وصف لثلاثة، على أن يكون {كلبهم} رفع برابع،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r7.speaker: أبو الفتح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r7.claim: Abu al-Fath rejects this too: 'fourth' is a participle intended in a past sense, so it cannot govern 'their dog' as a verb would.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p574/r7.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: (وهذا الوجه أيضا غير جائز، من قبل أن رابعهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r1.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r1.claim: Some take 'their dog is fourth' as a subject-predicate clause describing 'three,' as in 'these are three, their servant is fourth.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم: ({رابعهم كلبهم} مبتدأ وخبر، والجملة وصف لثلاثة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r2.speaker: أبو الفتح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r2.claim: Abu al-Fath says the clause-as-description analysis is not acceptable here: the conjunction before 'eighth' implies one before the earlier clauses too, so the clauses should be coordinated alike; it is omitted earlier because their pronouns link them to the first clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r2.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: (وهذا الوجه غير سائغ ولا مختار،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r3.speaker: أبو الفتح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r3.claim: He explains that the clauses 'fourth' and 'sixth' need no conjunction because they refer back to the initial 'three'; the conjunction appears in the final clause and is understood in the earlier ones.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r3.anchor: فكأنه قيل: سيقولون: ثلاثة ورابعهم كلبهم، ويقولون: خمسة وسادسهم كلبهم رجما بالغيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r4.claim: Abu Ali likewise says the first two clauses omit conjunction because they contain a reference to the preceding clause, understood as 'they are three.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي في هذه الآية فقال: (قوله: {رابعهم كلبهم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says adding waw before 'eighth' and omitting it earlier have the same effect.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r5.anchor: معنى قول أبي إسحاق: (دخول الواو في {وثامنهم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r6.claim: On this analysis, 'fourth' is coordinated with the predicate of the initial clause, while 'their dog' is an adjective of 'fourth.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p576/r6.anchor: وعلى ما قالوا قوله: {رابعهم} عطف على خبر الابتداء الذي هو ثلاثة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r1.claim: Rajm bi-l-ghayb means conjecturing and guessing; the author adduces Zuhayr's phrase 'al-hadith al-murajjam' as evidence for the sense of a guess cast out.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq glosses the phrase as speaking conjecturally and speculatively.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (أي تقولون ذلك رجما، أي ظنا وتخرصا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r3.claim: The bāʾ locates the conjecture: they speak about the youths while absent from them, without having witnessed the matter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r3.anchor: الباء هاهنا ظرف للرجم، والتأويل: يرجمون القول فيهم بالغيبة عنهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the waw before 'eighth' signals that the count has ended; Abu Ishaq similarly says it may signal completion of the account.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (حين وقعت الواو وانقطعت العدة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says waw may indicate that the story has ended and the matter is complete.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r5.anchor: أبو إسحاق فقال: (وقد يجوز أن يكون الواو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says he is among the few who know the Companions' number; in the report through al-Dahhak he names seven.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (أنا من ذلك القليل)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r7.claim: In the report through Ikrima, Ibn Abbas says there were seven.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r8.claim: In the report through Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas says they were seven or eight.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r8.anchor: وقال في رواية سعيد بن جبير: (كانوا سبعة أو ثمانية)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r9.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r9.claim: Ata al-Khurasani interprets the few who know as the People of the Book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r9.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء الخراساني: {ما يعلمهم إلا قليل}، يعني أهل الكتاب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r10.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r10.claim: Al-Suddi transmits Ibn Abbas as hoping to be among the few, guessing that there were three, and recounts their exchange about how long they had slept.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p578/r10.anchor: وروى السدي عن ابن عباس قال: (أرجو أن أكون من القليل، أظن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r1.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the permissible debate is to use what revelation conveyed in the Qur'an.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r2.speaker: سفيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r2.claim: Sufyan says the only permitted argument is what the Qur'an has related.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r2.anchor: وقال سفيان: (إلا بما قصصنا عليك في القرآن)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Dahhak say the account already related about the youths is sufficient.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك في قوله: {إلا مراء ظاهرا} (حسبك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says to tell disputants that their claim is wrong and that they do not know the youths' number, which only a few know.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: (المراء الظاهر: أن تقول لهم: ليس كما تقولون، ليس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r5.claim: The Arabic verb marā means to dispute or argue.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r5.anchor: ومعنى المراء في اللغة: الجدال، يقال: مارى يماري، مماراة ومراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq says not to speak beyond what was revealed, but to issue only the account's outwardly stated details.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (أي لا تأت في أمرهم بغير ما أوحي إليك،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r7.claim: The author concludes that apparent debate means arguing from revelation: the Qur'an says only a few know their number, as Ibn Zayd explains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p579/r7.anchor: فعلى ما قالوا المراء الظاهر هو: أن يجادلهم بما أنزل إليه من أنه لا يعلم عددهم إلا القليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r1.claim: 'Among them' refers to the Cave Companions, and 'them' means the Jews and People of the Book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r1.anchor: أي: في أصحاب الكهف {منهم}، أي: من اليهود وأهل الكتاب.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r2.claim: Al-Farra says two Najran Christian groups, Jacobites and Nestorians, came; the Prophet asked them about the youths' number and was then forbidden to ask.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: (هم فريقان أتوه من أهل نجران: يعقوبي ونسطوري، فسألهم النبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r3.claim: The authors infer from this verse that Muslims may not seek religious rulings from Jews or Christians.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581/r3.anchor: قال أصحابنا: (وهذا دليل على منع المسلمين من استفتاء اليهود والنصارى)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r1.claim: The dispute over the Cave youths’ number occurred in Medina after the Christian delegation from Najran arrived.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r1.anchor: فجرى ذلك بالمدينة حين قدم وفد نصارى نجران، فجرى ذكر أصحاب الكهف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r2.speaker: اليعقوبية
