WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r2.claim: The Jacobites said the youths were three, with the dog as the fourth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r2.anchor: فقالت اليعقوبية منهم: كانوا ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r3.speaker: النسطورية
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r3.claim: The Nestorians said the youths were five, with the dog as the sixth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r3.anchor: وقالت النسطورية: كانوا خمسة سادسهم كلبهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r4.speaker: المسلمون
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r4.claim: The Muslims said they were seven, with the dog as the eighth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r4.anchor: وقال المسلمون: كانوا سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r5.claim: Only a small number of people know their count.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r5.anchor: { قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم ما يعلمهم إلا قليل } من الناس

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas said he was among the few who knew, and then named seven youths.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أنا من ذلك القليل، ثم ذكرهم بأسمائهم فذكر سبعة.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r7.claim: Muhammad should avoid disputation except by the revealed outward account and should not ask any People of the Book about them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:22/r7.anchor: { فلا تمار } فلا تجادل في أصحاب الكهف { إلا مراء ظاهرا } بما أنزل عليك، أي: أفت في قصتهم بالظاهر الذي أنزل إليك، وقل: لا يعلمهم إلا قليل كما أنزل الله: { ما يعلمهم إلا قليل } ، { ولا تستفت فيهم } في أصحاب الكهف { منهم } من أهل الكتاب { أحدا }.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r1.claim: The Qur’an deliberately leaves the sleepers’ time, place, names, number, and—on the preferred view—duration unstated, giving only the event and cave setting while labeling conflicting numerical guesses speculation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r1.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm, bir hikmete binaen bunların nerede ve ne zaman yaşadıkları, sayıları, isimleri ve –tercih edilen görüşe göre– kaldıkları süre hakkında bilgi vermedi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r2.speaker: unnamed view
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r2.claim: One interpretation applies “guessing at the unseen” to the first two numbers; it treats the seven sleepers and an eighth dog as hinted by the statement that few know.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r2.anchor: “recmen bi’l-gayb” ifadesi ilk iki rakamla ilgilidir; “Onlar yedi kişidir; sekizincisi köpekleridir” diye ifade edilen üçüncü rakama gelince

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r3.speaker: İbn Abbas
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas said that he was among those who knew the sleepers’ number and that there were seven.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r3.anchor: İbn Abbas, kendisinin bunu bilenlerden olduğunu ve bu gençlerin yedi kişi olduğunu söylemiştir (İbn Kesîr, V, 144).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r4.claim: The command that God knows their number best recommends leaving such matters to divine knowledge, saying no more than revelation says, and avoiding useless speculation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r4.anchor: vahyin bildirdiğinden fazla bir şey söylememenin daha uygun olduğunu, böyle konular hakkında ileri geri söz söylemenin bir fayda sağlamayacağını ifade etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r5.claim: Hadith collections do not mention the story, while historical and exegetical works transmit extensive and differing accounts; neither Qur’an nor hadith specifies whether the youths were Christian or Jewish.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r5.anchor: Hadis kaynaklarında zikredilmemiş olan bu kıssa, tarih ve tefsir kitaplarında geniş ve farklı rivayetler şeklinde nakledilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r6.claim: Given the occasion of revelation, they may have lived before Jesus because Jewish scholars advised the polytheists to ask Muhammad about them; the etymology of “raqim” has also supported that dating for some.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r6.anchor: Kıssanın nüzûl sebebi dikkate alındığında bunların Hz. Îsâ’dan önce yaşamış olmaları muhtemeldir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r7.claim: Caves attributed to the sleepers are claimed in many countries and at Tarsus, Ephesus, and Afşin in Anatolia; Christian sources generally place the event at Ephesus, but the Qur’an focuses on its lessons, especially resurrection and the ultimate victory of believers in God and the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:22/r7.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm ise hikâyenin mesajı bakımından pek önemi olmayan bu bilgilerden ziyade, olayın üzerinde düşünülüp ibret alınması gereken yönlerini ön plana çıkarmıştır.

SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r1.claim: One explanation supplies an omitted transition: after answering the question about the cave, the Prophet is told to ask their number, so sīn marks the prediction; following coordinated verbs inherit its future force.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r1.anchor: قيل: إنما أتي بالسين في هذا لأن في الكلام طيا وإدماجا

SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r2.speaker: ابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r2.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin assimilates emphatic thāʾ into feminine tāʾ because their articulations are close, both are voiceless, and they follow a quiescent weak letter.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن " ثلاث " بإدغام الثاء المثلثة في تاء التأنيث

SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r3.claim: The clause rābiʿuhum kalbuhum is nominative as an adjective modifying thalātha.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r3.anchor: الجملة في محل رفع صفة ل " ثلاثة ".

SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r4.claim: In one narration Ibn Kathīr reads khamsata with fatḥa on the mīm, an idiom also found in ʿashara.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير في رواية بفتح الميم، وهي لغة كعشرة.

SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r5.speaker: ابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r5.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin is reported to read khamsa with kasra on khāʾ and mīm and assimilate its tāʾ into the sīn of sādisihim; the author calls this very heavy and suspects an error in the attribution. Another report has tanwīn assimilated into sīn without nasalization.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن بكسر الخاء والميم، وبإدغام التاء في السين

SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r6.claim: Thalātha, khamsa, and sabʿa predicate an omitted subject (‘they are three/five/seven’); the following clauses modify three and five, not ungoverned circumstantial clauses or demonstrative estimates, since no present group was indicated.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22/r6.anchor: و " ثلاثة " و " خمسة " و " سبعة " إخبار لمبتدأ مضمر، أي: هم ثلاثة

SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r1.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb has four parses: accusative of purpose, circumstantial ‘guessing,’ governed by yaqūlūn because it conveys that meaning, or governed by an implied cognate verb (‘they conjecture a conjecture’). Rajm originally means throwing small stones and came to mean conjecture.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { رجما بالغيب } فيه أربعة أوجه، أحدها: أنه مفعول من أجله؛

SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r2.speaker: زهير
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r2.claim: Zuhayr’s verse says war is not something merely conjectured or hearsay, witnessing murajjam in the sense ‘conjectured.’
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r2.anchor: قال زهير: 3139- وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتم

SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r3.claim: One account makes the wāw coordinate with ‘they are seven,’ recording two assertions by the disputants; another treats it as a new divine statement. Al-Zamakhsharī calls it an adjective-introducing emphatic wāw, which the Sheikh rejects because grammarians do not recognize it.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r3.anchor: أنها عاطفة، عطفت هذه الجملة على جملة قوله " هم سبعة "

SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r4.speaker: ابن خالويه
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r4.claim: Ibn Khālawayh and Abū Bakr, transmitter of ʿĀṣim, call it the ‘wāw of eight’: Quraysh allegedly inserted wāw when counting from seven to eight. Some applied this to Paradise’s eight gates versus Hell’s seven in 39:73.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r4.anchor: ذكر ذلك ابن خالويه وأبو بكر راوي عاصم.

SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r5.claim: A reading k-albihim means ‘owner of their dog’; some therefore supply ṣāḥib in the ordinary reading too.

SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r6.claim: The Sheikh supplies ‘persons’ as the omitted counted noun because rābiʿuhum means the dog makes them four; ‘men’ would mix incompatible counted kinds. The author praises this as sound.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#2/r6.anchor: فقدره الشيخ: ثلاثة أشخاص، قال: " وإنما قدرنا أشخاصا لأن رابعهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:22#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#3/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#3/r1.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says rābiʿuhum cannot function as an active participle governing an understood object because it describes a past event.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#3/r1.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " ولا يعمل اسم الفاعل هنا لأنه ماض ".

SAMIN-DURR:18:22#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#3/r2.claim: The author replies that it means the dog makes the group four and so governs implicitly; it works in the past by depicting the situation as present, like bāsiṭ.
SAMIN-DURR:18:22#3/r2.anchor: وليس كما زعم فإن المعنى على: يصير الكلب لهم أربعة، فهو ناصب

ASAD-NOTES:18:22#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:22#n31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:22#n31/r1.claim: The future tense in sayaqulun underscores the story's legendary character and makes speculation about details irrelevant to its ethical parable.
ASAD-NOTES:18:22#n31/r1.anchor: The future tense in sayaqulun points once again to the legendary character of the story as such

ASAD-NOTES:18:22#n32/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:22#n32/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:22#n32/r1.claim: Discussion should be limited to the self-evident ethical lesson of the story, alluding to the first paragraph of 18:21.
ASAD-NOTES:18:22#n32/r1.anchor: for the sake of the self-evident ethical lesson to be derived from their story

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r2.speaker: المفسرون
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r2.claim: Commentators, including al-Zamakhshari, take the waw before “and their dog was the eighth” as circumstantial and as confirming that this is the correct count.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r2.anchor: كما صرّح المفسرون أي كأنها تدل على أن الذين قالوا أن أصحاب الكهف كانوا سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r3.claim: The waw is circumstantial and stresses verification: it appears when descriptions are semantically distant, but is omitted when the descriptions are close in meaning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r3.anchor: الواو إذن هي واو الحال ولكنها أفادت التوكيد والتحقيق بأن هذا القول صحيح لأن الواو يؤتى بها إذا تباعد معنى الصفات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r4.claim: He illustrates distant descriptions joined by waw with “the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden,” and similar descriptions without waw with “slanderer, going about with calumnies.”
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p59/r4.anchor: وإذا اقترب معنى الصفات لا يؤتى بالواو

IBNMUJAHID:v1p402/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p402/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p402/r1.claim: Of 37 additional yāʾs in the sura, nine differ: Nāfiʿ opens all listed forms except the three maʿī ṣabran; Abū ʿAmr quiesces that trio and satجدني; Ibn Kathīr follows him except min dūnī awliyāʾ; Ḥafṣ opens the trio.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p402/r1.anchor: فى هذه السورة سبع وثلاثون ياء إضافة اختلفوا فى تسع منها قوله ﴿ ربي أعلم ﴾

QIRAAT-ER:18:22:20#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:22:20#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:22:20#1/r1.claim: Fatḥa on yāʾ lengthens the possessive pronunciation without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:18:22:20#1/r1.anchor: Variant adds fatḥa on yāʾ (rabbiya vs. rabbī) — phonetic lengthening of possessive

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses guessing at the unseen as making conjectures without knowledge.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ رجما بالغيب ﴾ قال قذفا بالظن

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r2.claim: Qatāda says Ibn ʿAbbās counted himself among the few and held that the sleepers were seven, with their dog eighth.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ﴿ ما يعلمهم إلا قليل ﴾ قال كان ابن عباس يقول أنا من القليل سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r3.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet need only rely on what has already been recounted and should not dispute further about the sleepers.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400#3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا ﴾ قال حسبك ما قد قصصنا عليك من شأنهم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r1.claim: Before ʿUthmān’s standardization, the dominant early Kufan reading was that of Ibn Masʿūd, whom ʿUmar had sent to teach; his pupils kept it in circulation afterward.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r1.anchor: وأما أهل الكوفة فكان الغالب على المتقدمين من أهلها قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه لأنه هو الذي بعث به

IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm names ʿAlqama, al-Aswad, Masrūq, al-Ḥārith b. Qays, ʿAmr b. Shurahbīl, and ʿUbayda al-Salmānī as Ibn Masʿūd’s companions who taught Qurʾān and issued rulings.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال كان أصحاب عبد الله الذين يقرئون الناس القرآن ويفتون علقمة والأسود ومسروق والحارث ابن قيس

IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r3.speaker: الأعمش
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash compares the rarity of Zayd’s reading among early Kufans to Ibn Masʿūd’s reading among his contemporaries, which only one or two recited.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r3.anchor: عن الأعمش قال أدركت أهل الكوفة وما قراءة زيد فيهم إلا كقراءة عبد الله فيكم اليوم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r4.speaker: مسروق
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r4.claim: Masrūq says Ibn Masʿūd taught in the mosque, and his reading remained the only one people in Kufa knew.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r4.anchor: عن مسلم عن مسروق قال كان عبد الله يقرئنا في المسجد تم تجلس بعده نثبت الناس

IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r5.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, named ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥabīb, was the first to teach in Kufa the reading standardized by ʿUthmān.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r5.anchor: وأول من أقرأ بالكوفة القراءة التي جمع عثمان رضي الله تعالى عنه الناس عليها أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي واسمه عبد الله بن حبيب

IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r6.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān taught in the Great Mosque for forty years, until his death during Bishr b. Marwān’s governorship.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r6.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق أن أبا عبد الرحمن كان يقرىء الناس في المسجد الأعظم أربعين سنة إلى أن توفي في ولاية بشر بن مروان

IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r7.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r7.claim: The source dates Bishr b. Marwān’s governorship to 73 AH.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p66/r7.anchor: وكانت ولاية بشر بن مروان سنة ثلاث وسبعين

IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r7.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r7.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r7.claim: The people saying how many sleepers there were are the Jewish rabbis who had instructed the Meccans to question the Prophet about them.
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r7.anchor: سيقولون 18: 21- 22 يعني أحبار يهود الذين أمروهم بالمسألة عنهم

IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r8.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r8.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r8.claim: The three- and five-person counts are guesses without knowledge; the text also reports seven and says God knows their number, with only a few knowing it.
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r8.anchor: ويقولون خمسة سادسهم كلبهم، رجما بالغيب 18: 22: أي لا علم لهم. ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم

IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r9.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r9.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r9.claim: Do not contend with them except superficially, and do not ask any of them about the sleepers because they have no knowledge.
IBNHISHAM:v1p305/r9.anchor: فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا 18: 22: أي لا تكابرهم. ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا

BURHAN:v4p440/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p440/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p440/r1.claim: The coordinating waw may occur without a repeated conjunction, as in the phrase about the eighth and its dog.
BURHAN:v4p440/r1.anchor: بل يجوز دخولها من غير تكرار قال تعالى ﴿ ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم

BURHAN:v4p440/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p440/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p440/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the waw emphasizes the adjective’s firm attachment to its noun, signaling an established quality; such a clause may qualify an indefinite noun.
BURHAN:v4p440/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري دخلت الواو لتأكيد لصوق الصفة بالموصوف الدالة على إن اتصافه بها أمر ثابت مستقر

BURHAN:v4p440/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p440/r3.speaker: جمال الدين بن مالك وأثير الدين
BURHAN:v4p440/r3.claim: Ibn Malik and Athir al-Din say al-Zamakhshari was alone in proposing this emphatic use of waw.
BURHAN:v4p440/r3.anchor: وقال الشيخ جمال الدين بن مالك في باب الاستثناء من شرح التسهيل وتابعه الشيخ أثير الدين إن الزمخشري تفرد بهذا القول

BURHAN:v4p440/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p440/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p440/r4.claim: The author rejects the claim that al-Zamakhshari was alone, since al-Azhari also recorded waw for emphasis.
BURHAN:v4p440/r4.anchor: إن الزمخشري تفرد بهذا القول وليس كذلك فقد ذكر الأزهري في الأزهرية

BURHAN:v4p440/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p440/r5.speaker: الأزهري
BURHAN:v4p440/r5.claim: Al-Azhari gives emphatic waw after illa in ordinary Arabic and cites Qur'anic examples of the construction.
BURHAN:v4p440/r5.anchor: ذكر الأزهري في الأزهرية فقال وتأتي الواو للتأكيد نحو ما رأيت رجلا إلا وعليه ثوب حسن

BURHAN:v2p415/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p415/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p415/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that wāw enters a descriptive clause to emphasize the attribute’s establishment, as it does in circumstantial clauses.
BURHAN:v2p415/r4.anchor: زعم الزمخشري انها تدخل على الجملة الواقعه صفة التأكيد ثبوت الصفة بالموصوف

BURHAN:v2p415/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p415/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p415/r5.claim: Al-Zarkashī rejects that analysis: the clause is circumstantial, since an exceptive construction with an omitted exception does not occur in adjectival clauses and village is general after illā.
BURHAN:v2p415/r5.anchor: والصحيح ان الجملة الموضوف بها لاتقترن بالواو لان الاستثناء المفرغ لايقع في الصفات

BURHAN:v3p246/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p246/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p246/r1.claim: Numerals are ordered naturally from each rank to the next higher one: two, three, four, and likewise three/four or five/six in the cited examples.
BURHAN:v3p246/r1.anchor: وكذلك جميع الأعداد كل مرتبة هي متقدمة على ما فوقها بالذات

ITQAN:v2p525/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p525/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v2p525/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says wāw can join an adjectival clause to emphasize that the attribute is established and closely attached to its subject; he takes the sleepers' dog phrase as an example.
ITQAN:v2p525/r2.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري أنها تدخل على الجملة الواقعة صفة لتأكيد ثبوت الصفة للموصوف ولصوقها بها

ITQAN:v2p525/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p525/r3.speaker: جماعة
ITQAN:v2p525/r3.claim: Some grammarians posit a “waw of eight,” claiming Arabs insert it after seven to mark a complete number and a new start; al-Suyuti rejects this, saying these examples all use ordinary conjunction.
ITQAN:v2p525/r3.anchor: والصواب عدم ثبوتها وأنها في الجميع للعطف

ITQAN:v2p550#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p550#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p550#2/r1.claim: Pronouns normally keep the same referent to avoid disorder in the wording, though the Qur'an can vary them when context requires.
ITQAN:v2p550#2/r1.anchor: الأصل توافق الضمائر في المرجع حذرا من التشتيت ولهذا لما جوز بعضهم

ITQAN:v2p550#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p550#2/r4.speaker: ثعلب
ITQAN:v2p550#2/r4.claim: Tha'lab and al-Mubarrad allow an exception to uniform pronoun reference here: “among them” refers to the People of the Cave, while “from them” refers to the Jews.
ITQAN:v2p550#2/r4.anchor: فإن ضمير فيهم لأصحاب الكهف ومنهم لليهود قاله ثعلب والمبرد

DAMGHANI:v1p433/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p433/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p433/r5.claim: الامتراء and المماراة mean disputing or arguing about something doubtful; in 18:22 it means do not argue with them beyond an evident argument.
DAMGHANI:v1p433/r5.anchor: الثانى : الامتراء والمماراة المحاجة فيما فيه مرية . قوله تعالى سورة مريم

BURHAN:v3p211/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p211/r3.speaker: الواحدي
BURHAN:v3p211/r3.claim: He compares سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم, without waw, to وثامنهم: the omitted waw may be licensed by close connection, or mark a resumed sentence.
BURHAN:v3p211/r3.anchor: ومثله ﴿ سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم ﴾ 5 ولم يقل ورابعهم كما قال ﴿ وثامنهم ﴾

BURHAN:v4p438/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p438/r3.speaker: ابن خالويه
BURHAN:v4p438/r3.claim: Ibn Khālawayh and others cite thāminuhum kalbuhum after two earlier counts without wāw, and the differing door descriptions of Paradise and Hell, as evidence for the eight-marker theory.
BURHAN:v4p438/r3.anchor: ونقل عن ابن خالويه وغيره ومثلوه بقوله تعالى ﴿ وثامنهم كلبهم ﴾

BURHAN:v2p114/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p114/r9.claim: The author adds Qur’anic phrases as examples of metrical coincidence, including night worship, charity, disputing, the flood, Abu Lahab, victory, conversion, and Qarun.

BURHAN:v1p106/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p106/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p106/r7.claim: The author adds that رجما بالغيب means conjecture, while rajm can also mean expulsion or cursing; رجيم is said of Satan for this reason.
BURHAN:v1p106/r7.anchor: أى ظنا والرجم أيضا الطرد واللعن ومنه قيل للشيطان رجيم

BURHAN:v3p135/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p135/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p135/r1.claim: Number predicates omit an initial pronoun, understood as they are three, five or seven; in the two-party example, one party is understood from the mention of another.
BURHAN:v3p135/r1.anchor: أي هم ثلاثة وهم خمسة وهم سبعة

BURHAN:v2p451/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p451/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p451/r6.claim: The claim that waaw enters adjectival clauses only after repeated adjectives is wrong; Zarkashi cites these examples and an ordinary Arabic sentence.
BURHAN:v2p451/r6.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنه لايؤتى بالواو في الصفات إلا إذا تكررت النعوت وليس كذلك ومنه قوله تعالى ﴿ ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم ﴾

ITQAN:v2p417/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p417/r13.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v2p417/r13.claim: Ibn Faris says rajm generally means killing, but la-arjumannaka means I will insult you and rajman bil-ghayb means conjecture.
ITQAN:v2p417/r13.anchor: وكل ما فيه من الرجم فهو القتل إلا ﴿ لأرجمنك ﴾ فمعناه لأشتمنك و ﴿ رجما بالغيب ﴾ أي ظنا

ITQAN:v4p470/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p470/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p470/r7.claim: Disputes over the Cave dog’s color or name, the cow part used, Noah’s ship dimensions, or the slain boy’s name have no use and need not be known.
ITQAN:v4p470/r7.anchor: وهذا القسم الذي لا يمكن معرفة صحيحه من ضعيفه عامته مما لا فائدة فيه ولا حاجة بنا إلى معرفته وذلك كاختلافهم في لون كلب أصحاب الكهف

DAMGHANI:v1p389/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p389/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p389/r5.claim: The few who know the number of the Companions of the Cave are identified as ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās.
DAMGHANI:v1p389/r5.anchor: القليل عبد الله بن العباس قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

DAMGHANI:v1p196/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p196/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p196/r8.claim: Rajm can mean conjecture, as in guessing about the number of the Companions of the Cave.
DAMGHANI:v1p196/r8.anchor: الرجم شبه الظن كقوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

DAMGHANI:v1p316/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p316/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p316/r6.claim: ʿIdda can mean a number or count, as in the count of months, sleepers, possessions, or people.
DAMGHANI:v1p316/r6.anchor: الرابع العدة العدد قوله سبحانه في سورة التوبة ان عدة الشهور عند الله اثنا عشر شهرا يعني عدد الشهور

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r7.claim: A fifth sense is speaking conjecturally about something unseen, according to Muqātil.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r7.anchor: والخامس : القول بالظن . ومنه قوله تعالى في

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r5.claim: A fourth sense is conjecture, also used of people who cast conjectures about the unseen in Sabaʾ.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r5.anchor: والرابع : الظن . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف :

FARRA:v1p93/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p93/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p93/r1.claim: The numbers in the reports ‘three, their dog fourth’ and the following alternatives are nominative because they report ‘they are three/five/seven,’ not accusative objects.
FARRA:v1p93/r1.anchor: لا يكون نصبا لأنه إخبار عنهم فيه أسماء مضمرة كقولك: هم ثلاثة، وهم خمسة.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r9.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r9.claim: A third use means some of the People of the Book; Ata gives this interpretation of the few who know the cave sleepers' number.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r9.anchor: في الكهف : ﴿ ما يعلمهم إلا قليل ﴾ ، قاله عطاء .

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r4.claim: Rajm also means conjecture, as in rajman bi al-ghayb: one figuratively throws a guess.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r4.anchor: ويوضع موضع الظن، ومنه قوله: رجما بالغيب

NASHR:v2p39/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p39/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان الضرير
NASHR:v2p39/r2.claim: Abū ʿUthmān al-Ḍarīr transmits imāla for the al-Māʾida forms, the al-Aʿrāf form, and fala tumāri in al-Kahf; his routes agree explicitly and in performance.
NASHR:v2p39/r2.anchor: فروى عنه أبو عثمان الضرير إمالتها وهذا مما اجتمعت عليه الطرق عن أبي عثمان نصا وأداء

NASHR:v2p39/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p39/r3.speaker: جعفر بن محمد النصيبي
NASHR:v2p39/r3.claim: Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad al-Naṣībī transmits fatḥ for the cited forms, and the source reports no disagreement from him on that transmission.
NASHR:v2p39/r3.anchor: وروى فتح الكلمات الثلاث جعفر بن محمد النصيبي
